fields.index: the object's index in the table kind selects. objective_target_destroyed reads byte 0 as the index into mechTable or gameThings.
fields.kind: which table index refers to: 1 tracked object, 2 mech, 4 gamething. objective_target_destroyed switches on byte 1 with exactly those cases (a tracked object always answers 0 there).

fields.tag: copied from arenaTag_AGP..arenaTag_CINS, in that order
fields.bytes: a DTBL total times that arena's item size - see arena_budget_build

fields.unlimitedAmmo: cheat_handle_command toggles it and posts 'Unlimited Ammo ON/OFF'. cockpit only decrements a weapon's ammo when it is clear or the mech is not the player's
fields.invulnerability: cheat_handle_command posts 'Invulnerability ON/OFF'. The sim consumers pair it with playerMechIndex, so it covers the player's mech only: mech_heat_update skips a random heat event, and ai_group_part1 skips the MASC malfunction roll, when it is set. ai_debug reads it without the player test, and ui_callbacks clears it in two places
fields.splashDamage: the targeting UI's key 0x78 toggles it and posts 'Splash Damage ON/OFF'
fields.collisionDamage: the targeting UI's key 0x79 toggles it and posts 'Collision Damage ON/OFF'. It gates the landing damage in mech_std_tick_terrain - downward speed past -0x102762 becomes mech_apply_damage on locations 8 and 7 - and also mech_collision_damage (formerly terrain_sub_020890) and obstacle_collision_damage (formerly terrain_sub_020a50), which difference two objects' velocities. CORRECTION: the simOptions note called this 'fall damage'. That was the landing consumer read alone; the game's own message and the two object-velocity consumers make falls one case of it
fields.heatTracking: cheat_handle_command and the targeting UI's key 0x7a both toggle it, posting 'Heat tracking ON/OFF' and 'Heat Tracking ON/OFF'. WHAT IT DOES, from its two consumers: OFF, mech_heat_update zeroes heatLevel and heatThisTick for the PLAYER'S mech every update, so the player never heats up or shuts down, while AI mechs are unaffected; ON, heat accumulates normally and environment_heat_update also adds heat from hot scenery (object type family 0x10). The options loader writes 1 as its default
fields.difficulty: 0 to 2 - the file is mw2dif.cfg. mech_config switches on it twice; the simOptions note has the values

fields.directory: this type's directory once project_load_directories has read it, null until then; project_resource_size and project_read_resource load all directories when they find it null.
fields.field_0x4: the projectTypeAux note: project_close frees it through projectFreeHook when non-null; nothing else reads or writes it.

fields.celId: the frame's CEL resource id, -1 for an empty entry. bitmap3d_add_frame (BMPJ) fills the first -1 entry of a block; bitmap3d_draw draws nothing for an id below 1, and bitmap3d_animate wraps to frame 0 at the first one
fields.field_0x2: NO CONSUMER FOUND, so left unnamed. bitmap3d_draw adds 1 to it every time it draws the frame and bitmap3d_reset zeroes it; nothing else touches it, directly or through bitmap3dFrames. A draw count nobody reads
fields.cel: the frame's CEL once loaded, or null. bitmap3d_draw uses it when set and otherwise calls cache_load_resource(mainProject, celId, CEL) and stores the result here, so each frame is loaded on first draw and then reused; the draw reads the CEL's first two ushorts as width and height and the pixels from +4. bitmap3d_reset nulls it WITHOUT releasing anything, and no cache_unlock or cache_release of a CEL appears anywhere, so whether the cache can purge a CEL out from under this pointer is not established

fields.tag: four characters, compared against the tag_* dwords (tag_PTBL, tag_STAR ...); project_chunk_exec dispatches on it
fields.size: the whole chunk including this header: project_next_chunk advances by it and refuses anything under 8. The handlers size their payload from it - path_table_load takes (size - 0x48) / 0x1c points, formation_table_load requires (size - 0x18) / 0xc == 5, star_table_load reads (size - 8) / 0x18 group records

fields.flags: 0x01 LABEL (args[0] is the state it starts), 0x02 LOOP START, 0x04 loop back unless animTarget is one of args[0..3] (a list ended by -1), 0x08 loop back always, 0x10 EVENT (raises MechEntity.motionFlags bit 1), 0x40 transition when animTarget == args[1], 0x80 transition to args[1] on any target other than the current animState
fields.flags2: 0x01 transition to args[2] when there is no target (animTarget -1), 0x02 ENTRY - the frame to enter at when coming from state args[3], 0x04 END of the animation, 0x08 STEP SOUND (raises motionFlags bit 3)
fields.args: signed state numbers whose meaning the flags pick: [0] the label's state, [1] a transition target, [2] the no-target transition, [3] the state an entry frame is entered from; with flags 0x04 all four are a -1-terminated list. Bytes 2 and 3 of the frame are not read and are 0 in all 771 frames of MW2.PRJ

fields.dx: x DIVISOR: the x offset is length / dx, and 0 means no x offset. Both consumers agree - mech_probe_ray (the obstacle probes) and point_around_target (the point dist from a target in its frame). Values are 0, +/-1 and +/-2
fields.dz: z DIVISOR, as dx: the z offset is length / dz. Read by the same two consumers, which printed it as DAT_00096378 while the table was untyped. +Z is straight ahead: entry 0 is (0, 1)

fields.offset: file offset of the resource's record. project_read_resource seeks to offset + the type's recordPrefix, skipping the 62-byte DATA record header.
fields.length: the record's length INCLUDING that header: project_resource_size returns length - recordPrefix, and project_read_resource reads exactly that many bytes. In MW2.PRJ it equals the DATA record's own length - 8 field plus 8, on the records checked.

fields.rowCount: rows the prevBehaviour search walks - read at 0x2ca7b as the loop bound
fields.nonStartRows: subtracted from rowCount for the first draw only (0x2ca19..0x2ca24): with prevBehaviour 0xff the start row is random_range(rowCount - nonStartRows). 7 in the mech set, so only rows 0..5 can start

fields.condition: what the other objective must have done, per objective_prereq_met: 1 finished either way (state 5 or 6), 2 Successful (5), 3 Failed (6); 0 ends the list (objective_is_active stops there). The installer codes it from the static letter: 'C' 1, 'S' 2, 'F' 3, else 0.
fields.objective: the other objective's index - objective_prereq_met multiplies it by 0xf7. Unaligned.
fields.table: the other objective's table - multiplied by 0x2e8a. So a prerequisite can name an objective in ANOTHER group's table.

fields.base: the block's memory, from cache_alloc(size) at the end of static_arena_init (0x34204). static_malloc returns base + (size - free)
fields.size: 0xffdc while static_arena_init is packing; once packing is done it is shrunk to size - free, the bytes actually claimed, and that is what is allocated
fields.free: bytes not yet handed out. Packing starts it at 0xffdc and subtracts each tag's budget; best fit picks the block with the SMALLEST free that still holds the tag. After packing it is reset to equal size, and static_malloc then counts it down

fields.condition: selects a slot in aiRuleConditions, which searches for something and returns an object handle or 0. Three other things key off this same word: ai_rules_rebuild stops appending when it reads 0, so 0 terminates a block; it pairs with operand1 as the duplicate key when merging blocks; and ai_rule_post_to_leader copies it into the leader's leaderRequest, so it doubles as the request code.
fields.operand1: first argument to the condition, resolved first through the sentinels: 0x40 ('@') means the mech's targetSecondary, 0x2a ('*') its targetPrimary and 0x25 ('%') zero; anything else is a literal. The ASCII sentinels are what suggest these records are assembled from text. Also half the duplicate key, and what ai_rules_run compares against leaderRequestArg.
fields.operand2: second argument to the condition, resolved through the same sentinels as operand1.
fields.action: selects a slot in aiRuleActions, called with the mech, this record and whatever handle the condition returned. A byte, not a word - the disassembly reads it with movzx from +6, which is why the decompiler rendered it as the low byte of the short at +6.
fields.nextState: the aiState the mech moves to once the rule fires - ai_rules_run hands it to ai_try_enter_state in EDX. Unaligned, at +7.
fields.targetOperand: a third operand, passed to ai_try_enter_state in EBX as the target to adopt on entering nextState. Unaligned, at +9, and the reason ai_try_enter_state has a third parameter at all. CORRECTION: this said it ran through 'the same sentinels as operand1'. 0x40 and 0x2a are the same, but 0x25 is NOT: for operand1/operand2 it resolves to zero (xor ebx, ebx at 0x21658; xor eax, eax at 0x2168f), while here it resolves to the HANDLE THE CONDITION RETURNED (mov eax, ebx at 0x2173a - EBX has held the condition's result since 0x216ec, and every aiRuleActions entry saves and restores it). So a rule with target '%' adopts whatever its condition found. 7 of the 32 shipped rules do (listing/ai_rules.txt, now printed as %found); the others name 0 (16), agp_myleader (5), @sec (3) or agp_home (1).

fields.block: index of the bitmap3dFrames block holding this slot's frames; bitmap3d_set_id (the BMID chunk) binds it
fields.frame: the frame showing, 0..31. bitmap3d_animate advances it by one per frame period, wrapping to 0 at 32 or at the first empty frame of the block; BMID resets it to 0
fields.ticksPerFrame: the frame period in 182 Hz ticks - bitmap3d_animate advances elapsed / ticksPerFrame frames and keeps the remainder. The BSEC chunk sets it, and bitmap3d_set_enable restores 0x2d (45 ticks, about a quarter of a second) if it is 0. An earlier note called it 'a factor multiplied into the per-tick expression': it is a divisor, and the multiply is putting the remainder back
fields.playMode: 0 stopped, 2 play once, any other non-zero value loop. bitmap3d_animate skips a slot at 0, and in mode 2 sets it back to 0 and rewinds to frame 0 the moment the frame wraps. Set by the BMEN chunk through bitmap3d_set_enable, and by effects as bitmap3d_set_enable(slot, 2) to play an effect's animation once
fields.state: bitmap3d_animate only runs a slot while this is >= 0; bitmap3d_reset leaves every slot at -2, which bitmap3d_set_enable also refuses. Set to 1 at load. The meaning of values other than -2 and non-negative is not established
fields.lastStepTick: the simTick the animation last stepped from. bitmap3d_animate stamps it with simTick the first time, and after advancing n frames sets it to simTick minus the leftover ticks, so timing does not drift

fields.duration: divisor setting the rate; larger is slower. It is a TIME CONSTANT, in 182 Hz ticks (ramp_start stores trunc(seconds * 182)), not a travel time: ramp_step closes (target - current) * elapsed / duration and then re-stamps lastTick, so each step removes that fraction of the REMAINING gap - an exponential approach, about 63 percent of the way after one duration and 95 after three, snapping to target once one step's elapsed time reaches duration. A port that makes these linear ramps will feel noticeably different

fields.type: 0 opens its submenu on Enter; 1 a value, Enter does nothing; 2 accept (Enter commits every control and pops the menu) - with 6 the menu's exit item, numbered 0 and drawn on the last row; 3 information, not numbered and skipped by the cursor; 4 a value committed on every step; 5 a value committed by its hotkey, and Enter backs out; 6 exit (Enter backs out)
fields.label: the text drawn after the item's number; 0 draws none
fields.draw: menuItemDrawFns[index]: (ctx, control, index, item, x, y, menu) - the widget drawn at the widget point, which also drives the control
fields.submenu: pushed by menu_draw on Enter over a type 0 item

fields.active: 0 free, 1 live - the only two values anything writes. destructible_register takes the first slot where it is 0 and stores 1; destructibles_blast_damage skips slots where it is 0; destructibles_update retires only slots where it is exactly 1 (cmp byte, 1 at 0x2b767). Releasing a slot zeroes it through the template.
fields.node: the scene node carrying the object's geometry. destructible_destroy spawns effect 7 at its position and frees its subtree; destructibles_blast_damage tests its position and radius against the blast; destructibles_update detaches it from the world on expiry. The same node is also given a fallingObjects slot at registration (falling_object_attach(node, 2)), so a destructible falls and tumbles while it can be shot, and every release path looks it up there and clears that slot too.
fields.registeredTick: simTick when destructible_register claimed the slot. Its one reader is destructibles_update: when simTick - registeredTick exceeds 0xe38 - 3640 ticks, 20 seconds at 182 Hz - the slot is retired quietly (no effect, no explosion), unless the flag at 0x9620c (playerOut (formerly playerEjectedDone)) is set. So wreckage lasts twenty seconds.
fields.hitPoints: 16.16, registered at 0x100000 = 16 points, and destroyed (destructible_destroy) the moment it goes NEGATIVE, so exactly 16 points of damage does not do it. Two consumers subtract: destructible_apply_damage, which projectile_update hands Projectile.damage << 16, and destructibles_blast_damage, which subtracts (rate * tickDelta) >> 16 - see that function's note on why blasts all but never destroy scenery.
fields.onRelease: a function called with the node whenever the slot gives its object up, for ANY reason: destructible_destroy after the explosion, destructibles_update on the 20-second expiry (0x2b7b3), and destructibles_reset (called once, in main's startup sequence beside gamething_table_reset); destructible_register also calls it at once when it cannot take a slot at all. Every caller tests it for null first. The two values passed in are debris_teardown (world-record debris) and 0x377e0 (mech wreckage - mech_detach_section_geometry and mech_crash_to_ground pass it). CORRECTION: the destructibles note called this 'a callback run when it dies'. Destruction is one of four paths into it; it is the object's cleanup, not a death handler.

fields.id: the context's id, which is also the MENU resource it opens (menu_load): main registers 4 (the main menu, and the pause gate game_update_pause watches), 5 (the user menu), 6, 7, 8 (the lance menus) and 3 (the credits, which nothing requests); calibration_menu_run registers 2
fields.request: 1 asks ui_context_dispatch to open the menu, 0 to close it
fields.record: the loaded module's MenuContext (menu_load); 0 once closed
fields.module: the LX block lx_module_load returned, freed by menu_close
fields.next: the next context in the list

fields.from: the behaviour this row follows: ai_choose_behaviour picks the row whose from equals MechEntity.prevBehaviour. With no previous behaviour (0xff) it instead returns the from of a random row among the first rowCount - nonStartRows
fields.choiceCount: how many of choices are live; the draw is choices[random_range(choiceCount)]
fields.choices: candidate next behaviours, aiBehaviourNames values. Duplicates are the weighting: the mech row for 4 ajmpin is {5, 5, 8}, adfa twice as likely as wbackp

fields.field_0x0: WRITE-ONLY as far as found. mech_load_config (formerly mech_dump_config) stores the bin's slot code / 100 here - the weaponTypes index of the weapon it feeds - and reads it back at once to look up the bin's rounds, damagePerRound and the two dwords below; that is the initialiser, not a consumer. No other reader: no exported body touches it, through loadout->ammo, MechWeapon.bin or raw stride-0x14 arithmetic. Left unnamed per the consumer rule
fields.rounds: remaining rounds; zeroed once the bin has gone up
fields.weaponIndex: index into MechLoadout.weapons of the weapon this feeds
fields.slotCode: the MechSection.slots entry that created this bin
fields.damagePerRound: multiplied by rounds to size the explosion
fields.field_0xc: WRITE-ONLY as far as found. mech_load_config (formerly mech_dump_config) copies weaponTypes[type].heatOnHit here. No reader found (same search as +0x00); the ammo explosion in mech_damage_slot uses only rounds, weaponIndex, slotCode and damagePerRound. Left unnamed per the consumer rule
fields.field_0x10: WRITE-ONLY as far as found. mech_load_config (formerly mech_dump_config) copies weaponTypes[type].heat here. No reader found (same search as +0x00). Left unnamed per the consumer rule. +0x08 is not written by the loader at all

fields.tag: four-character arena tag, one of arenaTag_AGP..arenaTag_ANFL. static_malloc and static_arena_reserve both search on it linearly up to arenaTagCount
fields.budget: bytes reserved for this tag. static_arena_reserve adds each mission's ArenaBudget.bytes into it; static_malloc reports system_error code 0x47 (SYSERR_SMMBADSIZE) when budget - used is smaller than the request - a WARNING, not fatal (listing/system_errors.txt; CORRECTION: this said it fatal_errors). static_arena_init sorts the table on it, largest first - the qsort comparator at 0x34370 returns b.budget - a.budget
fields.used: bytes handed out so far under this tag. Zeroed by static_arena_init, raised by every successful static_malloc
fields.block: index into arenaBlocks of the block this tag was packed into. static_malloc takes its memory from that block
fields.blockOffset: where this tag's share starts inside its block, written by static_arena_init as the block's size minus its free space at packing time. NOTHING READS IT: static_malloc hands out memory from the block's own free pointer, so allocations of different tags sharing a block interleave and only the per-tag byte total is enforced

fields.target: the angle it is heading for. ramp_angle_set_target is what writes it, and it wraps the value into +/-modulus/2 on the way in rather than storing it raw.
fields.current: the angle it is at now, always reduced modulo modulus
fields.duration: divisor setting the rate, in ticks; larger is slower. ramp_angle_start computes it as trunc(seconds * 182), via clib_fp_trunc.
fields.modulus: the angle that means a full circle. Every one of the five construction sites in the binary passes the literal 0x1680000, which is the full turn the rest of the sim uses - see MechEntity.heading. Nothing has been found that builds one of these with any other modulus, so whether the field exists to allow one is NOT established; only that it is read three times per step and never written except at construction.

fields.field_0x0: NO CONSUMER FOUND, so left unnamed. res_load_anim stores 1 when the ANIM was referenced with id -1 (by name) and 0 otherwise; nothing reads it
fields.frameCount: the ANIM's frame count (the resource's second dword). anim_player_step ends the animation when the frame index reaches it and bounds its label search by it
fields.channel: which scene-node channel the track drives: 0/1/2 translate x/y/z through scene_node_translate, 3/4/5 rotate pitch/yaw/roll through scene_node_rotate_euler - anim_player_step routes each step by it
fields.values: frameCount ints, the track's value per frame, pointing into the loaded resource. anim_player_step adds values[frame] to the task's valueLeft as each frame starts and spreads it over the frame
fields.frames: the ANIM's frame table, frameCount AnimFrame records after the last track in the resource; every track of one ANIM points at the same table

fields.canvas: the canvas the rectangle is on - defaultCanvas in every record seen; see the struct comment. READING THE C: the game copies these records whole with a five-dword rep movsd, and the decompiler shows that as a 5-iteration loop of dst->canvas = src->canvas; src = &src->left; dst = &dst->left - a whole-record copy, not a write of the canvas
fields.right: VWSP x + width - 1, INCLUSIVE; viewport_select takes right - left as the viewer's width. Confirmed independently by vfx_video's video set-up, which writes currentViewport as {&defaultCanvas, 0, 0, screen width - 1, screen height - 1}

fields.id: resource id within its type. cache_lookup matches it, and cache_load_resource stores it truncated to 16 bits
fields.locked: 1 while someone is using the resource, 0 when it may be evicted. cache_load_resource sets 1 on a fresh load and cache_lock sets it on a hit; cache_unlock clears it. The debug dump prints it as 'Lock='. It is only ever set to 0 or 1, so it is a flag, not a count: a second user's unlock makes the item purgeable under the first
fields.type: the four-character resource type (POLY, SNDS, ...), printed with %4s. Its four bytes plus id, mod 1009, are the hash bucket
fields.bucketNext: next item in the same hash bucket; cache_lookup, cache_free_item and cache_dump_entry all follow it
fields.purgeNewer: purge list: the neighbour nearer cachePurgeHead, i.e. unlocked more recently. cache_unlock pushes at the head by setting the old head's purgeNewer to the item; when cache_lock unlinks the tail, the tail becomes its purgeNewer. 0 while the item is locked
fields.purgeOlder: purge list: the neighbour nearer cachePurgeTail, i.e. unlocked earlier - the direction eviction comes from. cache_unlock sets it to the old head. 0 while the item is locked

fields.tag: the resource type, four characters ('POLY', 'TABL', 'MEK\0'): project_find_type compares 4 bytes here against the caller's tag.
fields.dirOffset: file offset of this type's directory; project_load_directories seeks here, and skips the type when it is 0.
fields.dirSize: the directory's size in bytes: project_load_directories allocates and reads exactly this much.
fields.field_0xc: not read by the game. In MW2.PRJ a second (offset, size) pair.
fields.recordPrefix: bytes to skip at the start of every record of this type - 62 for all 22 types in MW2.PRJ, the DATA record header. project_read_resource adds it to the entry's offset and both it and project_resource_size subtract it from the length (read as header + 0x22 + type * 0x18).
fields.field_0x16: not read by the game; 0x3a in every MW2.PRJ entry.

fields.x: copied from the file as-is; interpolated by task_object_track and set as the node's origin
fields.y: the vertical - task_object_track's rotate mode takes pitch from fixed_asin of this axis's delta
fields.z: the other horizontal - rotate mode takes heading from fixed_atan2(dx, dz)
fields.pitch: 16.16 degrees. The file stores whole degrees: path_table_load shifts this and the next two left by 16 and nothing else
fields.yaw: 16.16 degrees; replaced by the direction of travel in rotate mode
fields.duration: time to the next point - the divisor of the interpolation fraction, and summed across points to place the elapsed time

fields.cached: where the stream came from, and so how to release it. project_open_stream (formerly project_lookup_id) writes 0 when it read a loose file and 1 when it loaded the BWD resource from mainProject; project_item_release frees base when this is 0 and otherwise cache_releases resourceId as a BWD
fields.resourceId: the BWD resource id, or -1 for a loose file. Unaligned. project_item_release hands it to cache_release, and project_next_chunk's fatal error prints it as the ID in '%s ID %d'
fields.name: the stream's name: project_open_stream (formerly project_lookup_id) strncpys 8 characters from the reference and forces a NUL at +0xb. project_next_chunk prints it as the %s of '%s ID %d', and project_chunk_exec hands it to mission_mark_by_name, which is how an objective's targets come from the stream with its name
fields.streamLength: the BWD header's second dword. project_next_chunk stops when the next chunk's offset from base reaches it
fields.maxChunkSize: the BWD header's third dword. project_next_chunk calls system_error(0x2c) for a chunk larger than this, or smaller than 8
fields.base: the stream itself, starting with its BWD chunk - the cached resource or the loose file's buffer. project_next_chunk measures offsets from it; project_item_release frees it when cached is 0
fields.current: the chunk the reader is on: set to base by project_open_stream (formerly project_lookup_id), advanced by project_next_chunk by the chunk's size (12 for the BWD header), which returns it

fields.state: 0 as added, 2 once anim2d_draw has started it, 1 finished (anim2d_draw returns at once without drawing), 3 holding the last frame. 1 and 3 are only reached with flags bit 0
fields.frameCount: set when the SHP is first loaded, from vfx_shape_count(shp) - the dword at +4 of the SHP. anim2d_draw uses it as the loop modulus and as the one-shot end, and frameCount - 1 as the held frame. SNOWCLR, the one shipped ANM2's SHP, has 10
fields.ticksPerFrame: divisor of simTick - startTick; simTick runs at 182 Hz, so the one ANM2 in MW2.PRJ (18) plays at about 10 frames a second, so its 10-frame SHP loops once a second. From chunk +0xa
fields.startTick: simTick at the first draw; 0 means not started, and anim2d_draw stamps it and shows frame 0. A negative elapsed time is clamped to frame 0. anim2d_rewind (unreached) zeroes it
fields.flags: from chunk +8. bit 0: play once instead of looping; bit 1 (with bit 0): at the end, hold frameCount - 1 (state 3) instead of finishing (state 1); bit 3: anim2d_free the slot once finished. The one ANM2 in MW2.PRJ has 0, so it loops
fields.shpId: the SHP resource id, from chunk +0xe - the BASE (320x200) id. anim2d_draw loads id + assetVariant, so 175 SNOWCLR becomes 176 SNOWCLR6 at 640x480 and 177 SNOWCLRK at 1024x768. (The first note here called the bias only 'a likely display-variant bias'; screen_select_asset_variant has since established it)
fields.shp: the SHP from cache_load_resource, loaded on the first draw, or null. anim2d_draw passes it to vfx_shape_draw; anim2d_free cache_unlocks it. A failed load frees the slot

fields.lifetime: written into SimSlot.timeLeft as lifetime + tickDelta, and sim_slots_update counts that down by tickDelta, so it is a duration in the same ticks as everything else. 36 for a muzzle flash, 5460 for the nuke. Also handed to the palette fade as its length, so the flash lasts as long as the effect.
fields.screenFadePalette: -1 for none, otherwise a palette index passed to palette_fade_for_effect together with lifetime - a full-screen flash lasting as long as the effect. Only reached inside the scene-light branch (once misread as a camera cut), so only rows with lightsScene (formerly cameraCut) set use it.
fields.soundId: handed to sound_play_at with the offset from the viewer to the effect, guarded by soundId > 0. -1 on the muzzle flashes and on row 10, which does nothing at all.
fields.soundChance: -1 plays the sound every time; otherwise random_range(100) has to come up under it, so it is a percentage. Row 9 is the only row that uses it, at 10.
fields.lightsScene: when set, the effect becomes the SCENE LIGHT while it lives. This happens only when effectLightsAllowed is on and the effect is nearer the viewer than the current light. effect_spawn saves the viewer's lightPos, lightDirectional, ambientLight and the 0x9705c flag to 0x1538f8..0x15390c. It then sets lightPos to the effect, clears lightDirectional so it is a point light, lowers ambientLight by 10 (reset to 0x40 if that leaves 0..255), clears 0x9705c, and pauses lightObjectFollow. sim_slots_update puts it all back when the slot expires. So an explosion lights the faces turned toward it. The slot holding the light is recorded in lightEffectSlot and in its own SimSlot.ownsLight. CORRECTION: this was named cameraCut, read as 'the effect takes the camera', with the saved words taken for an aim point and two angles. Those words are the light: poly_light_intensity reads lightPos as the light source through viewer_latch_globals, and light_shade_level reads ambientLight. Nothing here moves or aims the camera.
fields.needsNode: the effect has geometry. It is half the test for whether a slot is claimed at all (the other half is lightsScene (formerly cameraCut)), and when set a free slot is only accepted if it already carries a scene node - the slots come pre-built per effect type rather than being created on demand. Zero only on row 10.
fields.areaQuery: sim_slots_update runs the proximity sweep for this slot every frame only when this is set: gamethings_near_point plus an AI notification, and the splash-damage query as well when simOptions+2 is on. So it marks the effects that act on what is near them rather than only being drawn. The radius comes from the node, not from here.

fields.offsetX: target for camKeyRampX, which camera_keys_update adds to viewer posX
fields.offsetY: target for camKeyRampY, added to viewer posY
fields.offsetZ: target for camKeyRampZ, added to viewer posZ
fields.offsetYaw: target for camKeyRampYaw, added to viewer yaw. camera_key_add takes it from the stack ([ebp+0x10]), after the four register arguments
fields.offsetPitch: target for camKeyRampPitch, added to viewer pitch. camera_key_add takes it in ECX. view_shake_impulse puts its magnitude here - 30x the vertical component of a straight-down impact, else 5 * (y - z) - so a hit nods the view
fields.offsetRoll: target for camKeyRampRoll, added to viewer roll. view_shake_impulse always passes 0 here and for offsetYaw
fields.ticks: how long this keyframe lasts, in 182 Hz ticks: camera_key_add stores round(seconds * 182.0) (the double at 0x91004), camera_keys_update moves to the next keyframe once cameraKeyElapsed reaches it, and camera_key_begin hands ticks * (1/182) (0x90ffc) back to ramp_start as the Ramp duration. Since a Ramp duration is a time constant, not a travel time (see Ramp.duration), a keyframe gets about 63 percent of the way to its offsets before the next one takes over

fields.field_0x0: not read by the game. In MW2.PRJ it is an INDX chunk header: 'INDX', length - 8, a dword, the type's tag again at +0xc, and at +0x10 a ushort equal to the entry count ((directory size - 0x16) / 8: 100 for TABL, 4385 for POLY).
fields.entries: indexed DIRECTLY by resource id - project_read_resource reads directory + 0x16 + id * 8 and project_resource_size + 0x1a + id * 8. Declared [1]; the real count is the directory's size. Entry 0 is (0, 0) in the data, and project_resource_size refuses id 0, so ids start at 1.

fields.classId: matched against GP chunk +0xa and stored as MechEntity.gamepieceClass (formerly objectState). The kill announcements name four: 1 mech, 2/4 vehicle, 5/8 aircraft, 3 a generic target - see MechEntity.gamepieceClass (formerly objectState). NAMED since: 1 mech, 2 truck, 3 artillery (the turrets), 4 tank, 5 helicopter, 6 wanderer (unused), 7 door, 8 transport aircraft (dropship) - see gamepieceClassNames and gamepieceClass for the evidence
fields.createLoadout: handed to mech_spawn, which calls it as (mechIndex, entity) once the entity exists. All three distinct targets allocate the MechLoadout and store it in MechEntity.loadout
fields.hooks: copied into MechEntity.hooks; [3] and [4] only for the player. SLOT 0 IS CALLED DIFFERENTLY: mech_dispatch_hook0 passes the MechEntity itself (EAX = mechTable[i], EDX = i), where the other drivers pass entity->loadout - so hooks[0], the create hook (mech_std_create, mech_alt_create, door_create), takes the entity and every other slot takes the MechLoadout

fields.viewX: view-space x, 4 x cm: clip_vertex_from_mesh dots (world - viewTranslation) with a view row and shifts right 27. clip_vertex_at_near_plane interpolates it to the near plane
fields.viewY: view-space y, same scale and the same two readers as viewX
fields.viewDepth: view-space depth, 4 x cm - copied from MeshVertex.viewDepth. clip_vertex_at_near_plane sets it to exactly viewNearClipScaled on the records it makes, and poly_emit_screen_vertices passes it on as the screen vertex's depth
fields.screenX: screen x, filled by the projection after clipping. poly_emit_screen_vertices reads it, and sends the polygon down the slow path (render_asm_sub_03d380) when it or screenY is outside +-0x3fff
fields.texU: texture u in 16.16 texels - MeshVertex.texU << 16, interpolated by the near clip and copied into the screen vertex by poly_emit_screen_vertices
fields.screenOutcode: written by clip_project_perspective: bit 1 screenX < viewLeft, 2 screenX > viewRight, 4 screenY < viewTop, 8 screenY > viewBottom. It is OR'd into 0x14fcd1 and AND'd into 0x14fcd0 per polygon, so the pair says whether any, and whether every, vertex is off screen
fields.projected: 1 once clip_project_perspective has filled screenX/screenY and screenOutcode; it tests this first and returns at once when set, so a record shared by several polygons is projected once. frame_arena_alloc_clip clears it on every new record. CORRECTION: this was declared unnamed with 'NO READER FOUND: no function in render/ reads a byte at +0x1d'. True of the functions Ghidra knew - the reader was code reached only through clipProjectHook, never made a function until tools/function_starts.csv recovered it

fields.field_0x0: WRITE-ONLY, meaning not established. falling_object_attach stores its second argument here - destructible_register passes 2, effect_spawn_fragments and mech_collide_obstacles pass 1 - and every release path zeroes it. Nothing reads it: a sweep of the disassembly of all nine functions that address this table finds byte accesses to +0x00 only as stores (0x2b3b5, 0x2b3d6, 0x2b8af, 0x2bb74, 0x2bd29, 0x2bd80). The fallingObjects note calls it a 'kind', which describes where the value comes from, not what it does; slot occupancy is tested on node, never on this byte.
fields.node: the scene node being simulated, and the slot's key. Null means the slot is free: falling_objects_full and falling_object_attach look for a null node, falling_object_find and destructible_destroy search for a given one, and falling_object_tick and falling_object_randomise_motion do nothing when it is null. falling_object_tick moves and rotates this node directly.
fields.velX: x velocity. falling_object_tick passes velX * tickDelta >> 16 (rounded) to scene_node_translate as its x displacement. falling_object_push adds its dx here. 16.16 cm per tick, like mech velocity. falling_object_randomise_motion throws debris at a standard deviation of 10 m/s per axis over the gravity in g, with the vertical mean 10 m/s up - see its note
fields.velY: vertical velocity, positive up. falling_object_tick adds accelY * tickDelta to it and moves the node by (velY + accelY * tickDelta / 2) * tickDelta >> 16 - the half-step form, exact for constant acceleration. Only while it is <= 0 is the terrain tested at all, so debris passes up through ground and lands coming down. On landing it becomes -(velY >> 2), a quarter-speed rebound, and on a random_range(2) roll is halved once more.
fields.velZ: z velocity, the counterpart of velX: scene_node_translate's z displacement, and falling_object_push's dz. On landing, velX and velZ are halved and reversed together, but only on the same random_range(2) roll that halves velY again - otherwise the object keeps its horizontal motion through the bounce.
fields.pitchRate: angular velocity about pitch. falling_object_tick passes pitchRate * tickDelta to scene_node_rotate_euler's first angle - note NO >> 16, unlike the linear velocities. Halved and reversed on every landing, with yawRate and rollRate. 16.16 degrees per tick; randomised with a standard deviation of 90 degrees a second (0x7e98 per tick).
fields.yawRate: angular velocity about yaw: scene_node_rotate_euler's second angle, yawRate * tickDelta.
fields.rollRate: angular velocity about roll: scene_node_rotate_euler's third angle, rollRate * tickDelta.
fields.accelY: vertical acceleration. falling_object_attach seeds it with -gravity, the global the mech movement uses as its vertical acceleration, and nothing else writes it except to clear it, so in practice every falling object falls at exactly gravity.

fields.node: the effect's node in the scene tree. effect_spawn sets its origin and orientation when it claims the slot, or hands it to effect_align_to_mount for the mount-attached effects, and sim_slots_update calls scene_subtree_move_to_alt_list (formerly scene_node_defer_free_subtree) on it when the slot expires. A free slot is only reusable for an effect with needsNode set if this is already non-null.
fields.x: handed to gamethings_near_point as the centre of the effect
fields.timeLeft: decremented by tickDelta every frame; at or below zero the slot runs its expiry path
fields.active: sim_slots_update skips the slot entirely when this is zero
fields.bitmapSlot: the bitmap3dTable slot of the sprite animation this effect plays, or -1 for none. CORRECTION: this was named lightRef, 'passed to the geom_luma lighting routines, so it identifies the light this effect drives'. The routines are geom_luma only by address: every consumer is a 3dbitmap call - bitmap3d_set_enable, which writes the slot's playMode, and bitmap3d_set_frame (formerly geom_luma_sub_037df0), which sets its frame - and nothing reads it as a light. The scene light is ownsLight's business (EffectType.lightsScene). THE LIFE OF IT: sim_tables_reset sets -1; the XPLO chunk sets it from chunk +0x0a and, when positive, starts the sprite with bitmap3d_set_enable(slot, 2), play once; effect_spawn, when it is not -1, rewinds it to frame 0 and plays it once; sim_slots_update and sim_slots_update's loop (once split off as sim_slots_update_tail), on expiry and when it is positive, stop it (playMode 0) and rewind it. QUIRK: the XPLO and expiry tests are > 0 but effect_spawn's is != -1, so an effect using 3dbitmap slot 0 would play on spawn and never be stopped
fields.ownsLight: set by effect_spawn on the one slot whose effect is currently the scene light (see EffectType.lightsScene), and the flag sim_slots_update tests before restoring the saved light. Cleared on expiry, in the same statement that puts lightEffectSlot back to -1. CORRECTION: named ownsCamera while the light was misread as a camera override.
fields.typeIndex: initialised to -1; an index into effectTypes - what the slot is currently showing. effect_spawn only ever reuses a slot whose typeIndex already matches the effect it is about to spawn, and counts how many nearby slots carry the same index to decide whether to spawn at all. CORRECTION: this was recorded as indexing 'a table of 28-byte descriptors at 0x0009f918'. The stride was right and the base was not: 0x9f918 is field +0x18 of the record, the one field sim_slots_update happens to read. The table starts at 0x9f900. The comparison against 0x16 is the split between world-placed effects and the mount-attached ones from 0x17 up.

fields.flags: bit 0: the widgets read the value through get every frame (else the cached +4); bit 3: set by menu_resolve_callbacks once the five indices below are code pointers, so a control shared by two items is resolved once. Bit 1 is set on every control in the shipped MENUs; no reader found
fields.value: the value the widget last showed; a widget writes it back every frame
fields.data: the widget's own record, read by the item's draw callback: menu_item_choice and menu_item_toggle {suffix callback, count, strings[count]}, menu_item_slider four SHP ids at [0], [2], [4], [6], menu_item_text_box {pane, text}
fields.selector: the argument every get/preview/commit/revert receives: a lance slot, a player command number (user_option_get), an Audio Ctrl selector (sound_option_get), a device index
fields.init: menuControlInitFns[index]: (menu, control) on the menu's first frame (state 1)
fields.preview: menuControlPreviewFns[index]: (selector, value) every frame the item is selected
fields.commit: menuControlCommitFns[index]: (selector, value) on accept (state 4), and on a step (type 4) or the item's hotkey (type 5)
fields.revert: menuControlRevertFns[index]: (selector) when the menu backs out (state 5)

fields.text: the slot's 0x100-byte text buffer (0xa4a2c, 0xa4b2c): message_post strncpy's up to 0xff bytes into it and forces a NUL at +0xff
fields.textX: the text's x in the pane: 0x28f (1%, a 16.16 fraction) in the image, pixels after message_bar_layout's layout_point_in_pane
fields.textY: the text's y in the pane: 0 in the image; message_bar_layout sets (pane height - font height) / 2
fields.inUse: 1 from message_post until message_bar_draw finds the time up; an empty slot is the first message_post takes
fields.priority: message_post's ECX; a new message replaces a busy slot only when this is not above its own
fields.fontId: FONT id (plus assetVariant) of the text; 1 in the image, message_post's EDX (1 when below 1)
fields.shpId: SHP id (plus assetVariant) of the bar drawn behind the text, shape 0: 0x4c in both slots; message_bar_layout also sizes the pane to it
fields.endTick: sim_stopwatch_elapsed() + ticks at message_post; the message shows while the stopwatch is below it
fields.pane: the slot's pane (0x95530, 0x95544 - whole-screen fractions in the image), laid out in pixels by message_bar_layout: slot 0 along the top of the screen, slot 1 along the bottom

fields.code: mesh_add_polygon writes poly_resolve_code(the WTBO polygon's code) here; see that function for what the code selects
fields.vertexCount: zeroed by mesh_add_polygon and bumped once per index by poly_add_index. Every reader loops over it: polygon_contains_point_xz, poly_overlaps_cell_xz, poly_compute_normal (3 takes the triangle path)
fields.indexOffset: byte offset from this record to its vertex-index BYTES: index i is the byte at polygon + indexOffset + i, and selects the vertex at vertexData + index * 0x2c. mesh_add_polygon stores it; poly_surface_height takes the first index as the plane's anchor vertex
fields.modelNormalX: the MODEL-space unit normal, 2.29 fixed point. poly_compute_normal writes it; mesh_transform_to_world reads it and rotates it into normalX/Y/Z
fields.normalX: the WORLD-space unit normal, 2.29: mesh_transform_to_world rotates the model normal into it (rotated, not translated). Readers: ray_hit_polygon (one-sided test, N . direction < 0) and poly_surface_height (plane solve, and >> 13 into hitNormalX/Y/Z as 16.16)
fields.normalY: normalY > 0 is 'faces up': the ground quadtree queries and walkmesh_point_below_scan only consider such polygons
fields.owner: the WorldObject this polygon belongs to; mesh_add_polygon stores it. READER: polygon_resolve_colour, the draw hook, reads it five times - the object's type word (+2), its objectClass (+0x24; the wireframe colour scheme switches on it), its flag word (& 0x10f) and the damage-level nibble of the flags ((flags & 0xff) >> 4) - so a polygon's drawn colour depends on its object's type, class and damage. (A first version of this note called +0x24 'its state field'; WorldObject already names it objectClass, which is what the typed body now shows.) CORRECTION: this was declared unnamed with 'NO READER FOUND'; the search had covered only the typed collision and clipping functions, and polygon_resolve_colour still takes its polygon as an int

fields.field_0x0: not checked by the game. 'DDIT' in MW2.PRJ. This buffer is the file from offset 0xc: project_file_open checks 'PROJ' at file offset 0, reads length from file offset 0x10, allocates length + 8 and reads that much from 0xc.
fields.length: the header chunk's length - 8, the chunk convention: project_file_open reads it (from the file, before this buffer exists) and allocates length + 8. 0x1806 in MW2.PRJ.
fields.typeCount: how many type entries follow; project_find_type and project_load_directories both bound their loops on it. 22 in MW2.PRJ.
fields.types: typeCount entries of 0x18 bytes. Declared [1]; the index a caller uses is project_find_type's result.

fields.state: 0 not yet drawn, 1 its first frame (the widgets run init), 2 idle, 3 enter the selected item's submenu, 4 accept (commit) and pop, 5 back out (revert) and pop - menu_key_action sets 3..5, menu_draw acts on them after the widgets have seen them
fields.title: drawn at the title point and underlined; 0 draws none
fields.slot: the lancemate a lance order menu commands (lance_point_menu_onload, lance_control_slot_init); no other reader
fields.count: items in use; the onload callbacks rewrite it, and keep spare item records after it
fields.onLoad: menuOnLoadFns[index]: (ctx, menu) once when the MENU loads; may rewrite the items
fields.items: the first of count records of 0x11 bytes (the list continues past this declaration)

fields.leaderMechIndex: set to -1 for none, otherwise a mech index; read back by group_get_leader
fields.memberCount: bounds every loop over members, and is the append index
fields.affiliation: which of the eight affiliations the star belongs to, 0..7 - an index into affiliationAllegiance. RENAMED from recordIndex, described as 'an offset into the table at 0x000fc604'. That table is 8 bytes: formationPresets ends at 0xfc604 and fallingObjects starts at 0xfc60c. star_table_load sets it from STAR record +0, and poly_resolve_code adds it to the polygon codes 0x00 and 0x14 while a member mech's mesh is being built
fields.field_0xc: WRITTEN, NEVER FOUND READ - left unnamed on purpose. The only writers are star_table_load (0x4dc93) and group_formations_load (0x4dcd3), each storing 0 right after group_set_formation_by_name. Three sweeps of every game function found no reader: the absolute address 0xfb570 (only those two stores); every function that takes groupTable's base 0xfb564, checked for a +0xc access (the two hits, in group_set_leader and star_assign_slots, are MechEntity.starSlot through a mechTable pointer, not the group); and typed MechGroup * locals, of which there are none. A reader through some other computed address would not show, so this is 'none found', not 'none exists'
fields.allegiance: 0 friendly, 1 enemy, 2 neutral - to the player. RENAMED from statusFlag ('written 0 or 1 alongside the 0x000fc604 table'). mech_allegiance returns it, and the values are fixed by what the game says: hud_target_readout_tick plays 'Friendly target identified' for 0, 'Enemy target of opportunity identified' for 1 and 'Neutral target identified' for 2, and mech_on_destroyed (formerly ai_log_new_leader) plays the 'Enemy ... destroyed' cues only for 1. star_table_load loads it from STAR record +4 and copies it into affiliationAllegiance[affiliation]; the GPS branch of project_chunk_exec forces the player's group to 0
fields.formation: which of the 0x20 formationPresets rows this star is flying. group_set_formation stores it and copies that row into formationTable[group]; when the group is the player's own it first speaks 'Formation change to ' plus echelon left / echelon right / line abreast / line astern / vee form / wedge, which is what names the field. group_reset clears it to 0.

fields.slots: 12 equipment/crit slots, printed as ' %3d' twelve times
fields.numSlots: how many of the twelve slots are occupied. mech_destroy_section loops exactly this many times destroying them, and the critical-hit roll refuses to do anything when it is zero.
fields.flags: printed as 'flags:%d'. The high byte is damage state, all of it set by mech_apply_damage and mech_destroy_section: 0x8000 means this section has taken a hit, 0x4000 that its armour is through - latched, so the breach warning sound plays once - and 0x2000 that the section is gone. The low byte splits into two nibbles selected by whether the hit landed front or rear, matching armorFront and armorRear; what the nibble values themselves mean is not established. RESOLVED by mech_load_config (formerly mech_dump_config), which writes them at load: it clears the low byte, then ORs in clamp((internal + armorFront) / 5, 0, 15) as the low nibble and clamp((internal + armorRear) / 5, 0, 15) << 4 as the high one, in chassis-file units before any scaling. They are the section's full-health totals in fifths, and every damage-level display divides by them: 15 - 3 * (internal + armour / armour scale) / (nibble << 16), clamped to 0..15, in hud_damage_diagram_draw, mech_apply_damage and netplay. So the level reaches 0 at full health and 15 when both are gone.

fields.track: animTracks[v3 + animTrackBase], the track this task plays
fields.node: the scene node it moves: the detail record's node, or the project object's, found by the id in the task's argument string. Null is animPlayerError 3 at INIT and makes every tick return 0
fields.entity: currentGamepiece at INIT - the mech whose motionFlags, animState, animTarget, gaitBand and animFrameTicks the task reads and, when controlling, writes. Null is animPlayerError 5
fields.baseFrameTicks: v1 of the task string, the unscaled frame time; anim_scale_by_gait(gaitBand, this) becomes entity->animFrameTicks. Zero is animPlayerError 6
fields.frameTimeLeft: ticks left in the current frame: each tick subtracts the elapsed time and the step is elapsed * valueLeft / frameTimeLeft; at or below zero the next frame starts and entity->animFrameTicks is added back
fields.valueLeft: how much of the current frame's track value is still to apply. Each tick applies a step clamped to it with its sign, so the frame lands exactly; a new frame adds track->values[frame]
fields.lastTick: the time of the previous tick (the tick message's third argument); elapsed is now minus this, and it is restamped every tick
fields.enabled: 1 when v2 of the task string was non-zero. A 0 here fails every tick with animPlayerError 4, which removes the task
fields.frame: the frame playing, -1 before the first and after the END flag or running off frameCount
fields.flags: bit 0 set when v2 was above 0x7f: this is the CONTROLLING track, the only one that sets and clears entity->motionFlags bits, publishes a reached label into animState and rewrites animFrameTicks. MW2.PRJ has exactly one per animated gamepiece

fields.modelX: MODEL-space position, cm. mesh_add_vertex writes it; mesh_transform_to_world reads it and writes worldX/Y/Z, rotated and translated; poly_compute_normal builds normals from it
fields.worldX: WORLD-space position, cm - the triple every collision reader and the clipper take (poly_clip_and_queue differences it against viewTranslationX/Y/Z, which is what fixes the axis order). Equal to the model position at load; mesh_transform_to_world keeps it current
fields.texU: texture coordinate along the CEL's first dimension, in texels (WTBO vertex +0xc). clip_vertex_from_mesh copies it << 16 into the clip record; see mesh_add_vertex for the whole chain and the data check
fields.texV: texture coordinate along the CEL's second dimension (WTBO vertex +0xe); as texU
fields.viewDepth: the view-space depth cached by poly_clip_and_queue once a frame, (world - viewTranslation) . viewDepthRow >> 27 - FOUR TIMES centimetres, compared with viewNearClipScaled/viewFarClipScaled, and the source of a polygon's depth-sort key
fields.clipRecord: this vertex's CLIP RECORD for the current frame, a cache. clip_vertex_from_mesh returns it when it is non-null; otherwise it takes a record from frame_arena_alloc_clip, fills it (view x and y through the view rows, viewDepth, texU/texV << 16) and stores the pointer here. object_draw_lod_mesh zeroes it on every vertex each frame, so the cache lasts one frame. CORRECTION: this field was declared unnamed with 'NO READER FOUND' - twice, in the increment that declared MeshVertex and the next. clip_vertex_from_mesh had not been searched; its own name note already said it caches the record at vertex +0x24
fields.flags: per-frame clip state set by poly_clip_and_queue: bit 4 marks viewDepth computed this frame (object_draw_lod_mesh clears it on every vertex before clipping), bit 1 nearer than the near plane, bit 2 beyond the far plane. The trivial reject drops a polygon when every vertex has bit 1, or every vertex bit 2

fields.minX: X range of everything under this node: the point queries return 0 when x < minX
fields.maxX: the point queries return 0 when x > maxX
fields.minY: quadtree_point_below returns 3 (below the tree, so inside) when y < minY
fields.maxY: quadtree_point_below only descends when y <= maxY; above it counts as outside
fields.minZ: Z range: the point queries return 0 when z < minZ
fields.maxZ: the point queries return 0 when z > maxZ. quadtree_raycast slab-tests the ray against the three pairs X, Y, Z in that order with ray_slab_intersect
fields.polyCount: polygons in this leaf; 0 means an INTERNAL node, and every query then recurses into children instead of testing polys
fields.children: the four quadrants, each possibly null. quadtree_ground_height and quadtree_point_below try them in order 0..3 and stop at the first that answers; quadtree_raycast_children keeps the NEAREST hit instead. terrain_alloc_quadtrees zeroes all four
fields.polys: polyCount polygon pointers, declared [1]. A leaf's queries take the FIRST upward-facing polygon (normal Y at polygon +0x18 positive) containing (x, z), not the highest; the raycast tries ray_hit_polygon on each

fields.startX: where the segment begins. ray_set_points takes this triple as its first three arguments and the end point as its next three; projectile_update passes the projectile's position at the top of the tick, weapon_build_fire_ray (formerly weapons_sub_0532c0) passes the scene position of the node the shot leaves from.
fields.endX: where it stops, and the field a cast writes its answer into: world_raycast clips the caller's ray to the nearest hit and projectile_update then reads +0x0c..+0x14 as the impact point. ray_set_length and ray_set_end_at_height both recompute it as start + unit * length.
fields.dx: end - start, kept in step with both points by every routine that moves either of them. ray_normalise reads this triple and nothing else.
fields.unitX: the direction as a 16.16 unit vector: ray_normalise divides each delta component by length after shifting it left 0x10, and ray_set_length multiplies back by a length and shifts right 0x10 with rounding. Stale whenever normalised is zero.
fields.length: the cached length of the segment, and the number ray_length hands back. ray_set_length treats it as the value to impose; mech_update_aim_range (formerly weapons_sub_053190) reads it after a cast as the range to whatever the sight is on, flooring it at 2000.
fields.normalised: which routine last filled in unit and length, not a plain boolean. 0 means neither has: ray_length and ray_normalise both test for 0 and recompute. 1 is ray_normalise's octagonal approximation, max + (mid + min) / 4 with no square root. 2 is ray_normalise_exact's x87 result, and that routine tests for != 2 rather than == 0 so it will upgrade a 1 in place. ray_set_end keeps the distinction: it zeroes the flag, then re-runs whichever routine the old value named.

fields.flags: a bitfield, loaded whole from the project record (word at its +0x1c) and thereafter only masked. Two bits are established. Bit 2 (0x4) is DESTROYED: gamething_apply_damage refuses to damage a thing that has it, gamething_destroy returns early rather than scoring the kill twice, the proximity scan and the projectile tracker both skip it, and netplay packs exactly this bit for all 254 things into a bitstream one bit each - which is the set of facts a second player has to be told about. Bit 5 (0x20) is IDENTIFIED, the same bit and the same meaning as TrackedObject.flags 0x20 and MechEntity.flags 0x20: ai_validate_current_target sets it, beside seenByGroups, the first time the player inspects the thing from inside range, and the targeting readout prints the real name once it is set. CORRECTION: this said the readout prints 'Unknown' while 0x20 is clear. Read from hud_target_readout_tick, recovered from a bad function start, the name is withheld only when 0x20 is clear AND 0x100 is set, identically for trackedObjects, mechTable and gameThings. A thing without 0x100 shows its name straight away. In its place a mech or navpoint shows 'Unknown' and a gamething shows hiddenText. So 0x100 is the conceal-name-until-identified bit as far as its only reader goes, this readout. (CORRECTION: this first said 'and a copy of it at unsorted.c'. That file is a stale export from the initial commit that no run regenerates, and the 'copy' was its FUN_0002fcb3, the same phantom function.) NO SOURCE OF 0x100 WAS FOUND: no GT chunk and no NAVP chunk in MW2.PRJ loads it, and no store of it was found in the decompiled C, so in the shipped missions the concealment path may never run. A linear disassembly sweep was incomplete, so this is not a proof. Bit 6 (0x40) makes gamething_destroy call into mission_config - mission_event_nop, an EMPTY function, so the bit does nothing in this build - and bits 0x1e and 0x100 are each tested somewhere, but what they mean is NOT established. Bit 15 (0x8000) is DEBRIS (an earlier version of this note listed it as unestablished too). Its three readers all act on the world record the thing is linked to: world_record_build skips building it while debrisEnabled is 0 or fallingObjects is full, and gamething_destroy_world_record and world_records_propagate - the two places a hidden record gets geometry - hand its scene subtree to destructibles_register_subtree with debris_teardown as the callback and release the record with world_record_release_subtree. So the piece stops being static scenery the moment it appears and becomes loose, shootable geometry, as a wrecked mech's parts do. THE DATA AGREES: all 1070 GT chunks in MW2.PRJ with 0x8000 place an OBJ whose parent is some GT's REPLACEMENT record (the one that starts hidden and appears when the thing is destroyed), so the debris shows up exactly when its structure is wrecked; 1052 of them have hitPoints 0 and the name 'none'. See listing/gamethings.txt. THE HIGH BYTE carries the same targeting bits as MechEntity.flags - ai_validate_gamething applies the same three rules to a gamething the player is targeting: neither 0x0400 nor 0x1000 (mask 0x14 of the high byte) and target cycling skips it (-5, unless playerTargetFromReticle), 0x0800 makes it never targetable by the player, and without 0x1000 it is refused (-7) beyond slant range 0x2ab98. Which gamethings carry them is in the word at the record's +0x1c; they are not decoded in listing/gamethings.txt.
fields.seenByGroups: bit per group, set as 1 << (mech->groupId & 0x1f) when a group first identifies this thing - the same statement, on the same line of ai_validate_current_target, that writes TrackedObject.seenByGroups for a tracked object and MechEntity.seenByGroups for a mech.
fields.geomIndex: index of this thing's world-object record, or -1 for none. CORRECTION: this was typed as SceneNode * and called 'node', on the grounds that it was 'handed straight to scene_node_get_world_pos'. It is not. Every consumer passes it to world_object_node, world_object_get_pos or world_record_object (formerly geom_poly_sub_0367c0), and all three bounds-check it against worldObjectCount and index worldRecords. The SceneNode * lives at WorldRecord.node (+0x20), which is what world_object_node returns and what world_object_get_pos eventually calls scene_node_get_world_pos on. The -1 sentinel was the tell: an index, not a pointer. (A later correction: this note first put the table at 0x101e9c and the node at +0x14 - the same byte counted from a base 0xc too high. The table is worldRecords at 0x101e90.)
fields.hitPoints: what is left of the thing. Loaded from the project record (the signed word at its +0x18) and reduced by gamething_apply_damage, whose second argument is Projectile.damage at the call site in projectile_update; at or below zero it is clamped to zero, an explosion is spawned and gamething_destroy runs. Zero also reads as 'do not damage this at all', since the same test gates entry.
fields.affiliation: 0..7, or negative for none - the same index MechGroup.affiliation holds. RENAMED from recordIndex ('an offset into the table at 0xfc604'). The GT branch of project_chunk_exec copies it from the last AFFL chunk (keyword affiliation), which starts each interpreter run at -1. gamething_allegiance reads affiliationAllegiance through it and answers 2, neutral, when it is negative; poly_resolve_code adds it to polygon codes 0x00 and 0x14 when the thing's mesh is built
fields.range: the distance inside which the player can identify this thing. ai_validate_current_target compares it as mech->targetDistance < range + 20000, which is the identical statement it uses with MechLoadout.range for a mech and with TrackedObject.range for a tracked object. Written from +0x40 of the scene node world_object_node returns, so the figure comes from the geometry rather than the project record.
fields.name: the thing's display name, strncpy'd 0x16 bytes out of the project record with the byte at +0x29 forced to NUL. The targeting readout prints it once flags bit 0x20 is set, and falls back to the literal "Installation" when it is empty. It is one of a pair: a second 22-byte string follows at +0x2a, now named nameAlt. CORRECTION: this used to end "Nothing in the decompiled code reads it, so it is left as padding rather than named." Something does. hud_target_readout_tick dispatches on the handle type and reads gameThings + index * 0x40 + 0x2a for type 0x400, exactly as it reads MechEntity.nameAlt for 0x200 and trackedObjects + 0x3e for 0x100. The reason it was missed is that every one of those three reads is written as a bare base + index * stride + offset expression, so grepping the field name finds none of them.
fields.nameAlt: the second of the two 22-byte strings every named object carries. Loaded by the same strncpy pair as name, 22 bytes further into the same project record, and terminated by a NUL forced at its last byte - it ends exactly where the record does. The targeting readout displays it through the same method slot (+0x58) as name, but from a different branch: that one dispatches on the handle type to name, this one to nameAlt, and it plays sound 0xdc as it does so. WHAT DISTINGUISHES IT FROM name IS NOT ESTABLISHED - only that the game keeps two strings per object and shows them in different places.

fields.owner: the mechTable index this part belongs to; -1 empty, -2 made but not yet claimed. detail_record_set creates every record with -2, and detail_records_claim, run by the GP chunk right after mech_spawn, gives every -2 record the new mech's index. So the OBJs of a REPR nest belong to the next GP in the file. CONSUMER: detail_record_build parents the part under mechTable[owner]->node and stamps owner into WorldObject.index, and mech_apply_detail_level and mech_build_detail_records pick a mech's records by it.
fields.builtLevel: the detail level currently built, or -1. detail_record_build sets it to -1 before loading and to the level after success; detail_record_drop_level and mech_build_detail_records destroy the object only when it matches the level they were given.
fields.polyIds: the POLY resource for each of the five detail levels, slot [level]. detail_record_build hands polyIds[level] to cache_load_resource(..., "POLY"). detail_record_set fills forward, so a part with fewer levels repeats its last mesh.
fields.parent: -2 to hang this part directly under the owner mech's node, otherwise the index of another DetailRecord whose node - or its object's node when it has none - becomes the parent. detail_record_build reads it that way. detail_record_set maps a -1 argument to -2.
fields.location: the mech section this part belongs to, stored by the OBJL chunk (keyword objloc) through detail_record_set_location. detail_record_build copies it into WorldObject.hitLocation, which is what projectile_update sends to mech_apply_damage as the location hit. DEFAULT 0, written by detail_record_set and detail_records_reset, for a part no OBJL names, and 0 has two consumers: mech_apply_damage refuses any location below 1 or above 8 (0x263b1..0x263bd jump to its exit), so a round that strikes such a part - a decal, a dummy node, a rotor - does no damage; and mech_apply_detail_level frees such a part instead of rebuilding it once the owner's flags bit 2 is set, so unlocated parts are the ones missing from a wreck. IN MW2.PRJ (tools/dump_objloc.py, listing/objloc.txt): over all 54 gamepieces with OBJL chunks, 468 parts are located - head 33, CT 160, RA 56, LA 55, RL 78, LL 86 - and 374 are not. NO PART IS LOCATED AT 2 OR 4, the side torsos: a mech's upper-body mesh (TW1_HEAD on the Timber Wolf) is its CT and its cockpit glass (WINSH) its head. See mech_apply_damage for what that does to where weapon hits land.
fields.object: the WorldObject built for the current level, or null. detail_record_build destroys the old one before loading and carries its WorldObject.flags bits 0x7ef0 over to the new one (object_get_state_flags (formerly geom_luma_sub_0386f0) reads them, object_set_state_flags (formerly geom_luma_sub_0386d0) merges them in and sets 0x8000). It leaves a family-0x50 (destructible) object alone and returns at once.
fields.node: the part's scene node, created on the first build as a child of the parent (see parent) and then reused across levels. detail_record_node returns it.
fields.originX: the part's position relative to its parent. detail_record_build passes the three to scene_node_set_origin - on a branch gated by a register the decompiler could not follow, so when it is skipped is not established. Set from detail_record_set's arguments; the reset zeroes them.
fields.typeCodes: one short per detail level, filled forward like polyIds. detail_record_build masks typeCodes[level] with 0xf0 and gives the object type (that | 0x100) - the family nibble under the mech class bit WorldObject.type documents. Family 0x70 is taken off the world chain and 0xa0 stamps 0x1a0 over the subtree; the other families are not established.
fields.released: non-zero once the part has been blown off and its debris torn down. CONSUMER: detail_record_build does nothing at all for a record with this set - no rebuild at any level - so a lost limb stays lost through later level-of-detail changes. WRITERS: detail_record_release_node sets 1 (and destroys the object and sets builtLevel -1) when the debris node it was registered with is released - the onRelease that mech_detach_section_geometry and mech_crash_to_ground hand to the destructibles; detail_record_set and detail_records_reset clear it.

fields.lodKey: the level-of-detail switch distance: object_draw_lod_mesh keeps the last mesh whose lodKey * Viewer.lodScale is within the object's view depth, and object_add_mesh keeps meshList sorted ascending by it
fields.vertexCount: zeroed by object_add_mesh; mesh_add_vertex counts it up, and object_build_ground_quadtree and the walkmesh methods read it as the vertex count
fields.polygonCount: zeroed by object_add_mesh; mesh_raycast_all loops over this many polygons, as do the ground quadtree builder and the walkmesh methods
fields.polygonOffset: byte offset of the polygon table from the block: object_add_mesh stores 0x18 + vertices * 0x2c, masked to 16 bits. mesh_raycast_all reads polygon i at block + polygonOffset + i * 0x24
fields.next: the next block in WorldObject.meshList, in ascending lodKey order - object_add_mesh links through it, object_free follows it to free
fields.transformVersion: the WorldObject.transformVersion this mesh's world vertices were last computed at: object_refresh_mesh stores the object's value here, and object_draw_lod_mesh and object_compute_bounds refresh the mesh whenever the two differ
fields.field_0x14: zeroed by object_add_mesh; NO READER FOUND, so left unnamed. The +0x10 and +0x14 reads in object_compute_bounds go through a pointer reused by then for coordinates, not through the header. Second search, after MeshVertex.clipRecord and MeshPolygon.owner both turned out to have readers the first search missed: with meshList, currentMesh and every mesh parameter now typed MeshBlock *, no function renders a read of it. A reader holding the block as an untyped int would still not show
fields.vertices: the vertex array: vertexCount MeshVertex records from here, then the polygons at polygonOffset. Declared [1]; the real count is vertexCount. RENAMED from vertexData, a 0x2c-byte placeholder that existed only so that object_build_ground_quadtree's reads of vertex 0's position at mesh +0x24/+0x28/+0x2c did not render as a second MeshBlock; with MeshVertex declared those are vertices[0].worldX/Y/Z

fields.flags: the object's flag word. Four bits are established, all from the list code. 0x1000 makes object_link hang it under altRootNode instead of worldRootNode. 0x0800 says the object is NOT on the world chain: object_add_to_world clears it on the way in, and object_link SETS that bit itself when the int at +0x24 is 4, three lines before it tests it. 0x0010 is the in-world bit: object_move_to_alt_list (formerly object_defer_free) refuses an object that already has it and sets it to make itself idempotent, object_move_to_world_list (formerly object_remove_and_defer_free) requires it and clears it. CORRECTION, two errors in that sentence: (1) the bit those two functions test and write is 0x1000, not 0x0010 - both read flags >> 8 & 0x10 and write the HIGH byte, which was misread as the low one; (2) it does not mean in-world. It is the same 0x1000 that makes object_link choose altRootNode, above: the setter moves the object onto altRootNode's list, the clearer back onto worldRootNode's, and scenery_c0_set_visible sets it exactly when it parks scenery to hide it. So 0x1000 set means ON THE ALT LIST. What 0x0010 itself means is not established by these functions. RESOLVED: 0x0010 is bit 4, the LOWEST BIT OF THE DAMAGE LEVEL in bits 4-7 below ((flags & 0xf0) >> 4), with no meaning of its own - nothing tests it alone, and object_set_state_flags carries it with the rest of the level in its 0x7ef0 mask. BIT 0x0200 IS BOUNDS VALID: object_ensure_bounds computes the box into bounds and sets it, and returns at once while it is set; object_update_world_pos clears it on every position update, so the box is recomputed lazily after the object moves. RE-CHECKED after that error, against the code, for the same high/low-byte slip: 0x0800 (object_add_to_world and object_remove_from_world test flags >> 8 & 8), 0x0100 (render_object_list tests flags & 0x100), bits 4-7 ((flags & 0xf0) >> 4, written as level << 4), 0x8000 (set as high byte | 0x80) and bits 0-3 with 8 (polygon_resolve_colour masks flags & 0x10f) are all as stated. 0x4000 is what the three sentinels are born with. 0x0100 is DRAW DEPTH-SORTED: render_object_list does not draw such an object in its pass but queues it with its depth, and render_draw_depth_sorted draws the queue afterwards, farthest first (depth grows away from the eye, per object_view_cull). PRECISELY: the queue is walkDrawList, which also receives every ordinary object's polygons during the walk, so an ordinary object's polygons are sorted INDIVIDUALLY among all others, while a 0x100 object is sorted AS A UNIT at its object depth and its polygons, generated only when render_draw_depth_sorted reaches it, are sorted among themselves and stay together. BIT 0x8000 is what tells the two kinds of entry apart there: every WorldObject has it (object_create, object_apply_load_flags and object_set_state_flags all set it), while a polygon draw record starts with its clipped-vertex count, at most 20 (the ushort the clipper stores at record +0, 0x3e469). IN THE SHIPPED DATA NO OBJECT CARRIES 0x100, so this path is never exercised. An object gets it only through its load flags (object_apply_load_flags), and every source of those is accounted for: OBJ chunks (+0x32) - none of the 12182 in MW2.PRJ sets 0x100; world records, whose flags bits 0-8 are that same OBJ value (project_obj_exec pushes local_2c, the chunk's +0x32, as world_record_define's flags argument - [ebp'+0x5a] with ebp' = ebp - 0x86, the frame the rep movsd of the chunk's +0xe block at 0x4e282 fixes); detail_record_build passes 0 and quadtree_debug_draw 4. So in practice walkDrawList holds only polygon records, and the x4 key mismatch never arises; a port can treat 0x100 as unused, or implement it as the code does. Where the bit comes from is known: object_apply_load_flags copies it, with bits 0-3, from the world record's or OBJ chunk's load flags. BITS 4-7 are a per-part DAMAGE LEVEL, 0 to 15: scene_subtree_raise_damage_level writes level << 4 through object_set_state_flags, raising it only, with mech_apply_damage's level of 15 - ((armour / scale + internal) * 3) / (section max << 16) for the section's parts. detail_record_build keeps bits 0x7ef0 across a rebuild, so the damage survives a change of detail level. The renderer reads it in polygon_resolve_colour: for a mech (type 0x100) or destructible (family 0x50) it scales each polygon's shade by (16 - level) / 16, or lifts it towards 15 when damageShadeRaises is set; the wireframe view also colours mechs by it. (This said 'how the renderer reads it is not traced' until that function was read.) BITS 0-3 come from the load flags (see polyLoadFlags for the per-mesh values in the data: 1 clan-colour screens, 2 T*CST* meshes, 4 panels). RESOLVED since, from their one consumer: render_object_list latches each object's flags word into polySortFlags (mov ax, [ebx] / mov [0x14fcc0], eax at 0x3cfaa..0x3cfb3) and the polygon clipper poly_clip_and_queue picks each polygon's depth-sort key from it (0x3e46c..0x3e501): bit 1 (0x2) the MEAN of its clipped vertices' depths, else bit 2 (0x4) the MINIMUM (nearest point), else the MAXIMUM (farthest point); and bit 0 (0x1) ORs 0x40000000 into the key, which puts the polygon ahead of every other in polyDrawList's descending order - drawn FIRST, so always BEHIND. Bit 3 (0x8) is tested by nothing and set by no OBJ chunk. The data fits (listing/objects.txt): bit 0 is on the clan-colour *SCR1 screens and T_1GPL plates, backdrops; bit 1 on large structures (T*CST*, S_1BLD) and fire and smoke; bit 2 most often on lasers, bullets, explosions and jet flames (LAS*, BUL*, XPL*, JET*), besides the panel meshes - effects that should read as in front. FOR A PORT: painter's-algorithm hints; with a depth buffer, bit 0 (always behind) and the order of translucent effects are what still matter. CORRECTION of the text before this: it said what they select is not established. The rest is unread.
fields.type: the class and family word, and the one field with consumers in four modules. Bits 8-11 are the class: 0x100 mech, 0x200 gamething. projectile_update settles those - on 0x100 it reads the index at +0x14 as a mechTable slot and calls mech_apply_damage, on 0x200 it calls gamething_apply_damage on the object itself. Bits 4-7 are a separate family code that readers mask with 0xf0; 0x50 is destructible, by the same dispatcher calling destructible_apply_damage. The class bits are the handle type nibble shifted down one place - mech is 0x200 in an object handle and 0x100 here - which is the pairing mech_has_line_of_fire performs. The game's own altTypeLetters table reads these bits and agrees: p for mech, t for gamething. BIT 0x400 is POOLED PROJECTILE GEOMETRY. Its one writer is the BTHG chunk in project_chunk_exec: when it gives a projectiles[] slot the scene node of a project object, it calls scene_subtree_set_object_type(node, 0x400), which REPLACES the word on every object in the subtree - so such objects carry exactly 0x400, no class bits and family 0. No other source has it: none of the 12182 OBJ chunks in MW2.PRJ does (their words are 0 plus a family, with 0x800 the only class bit, on 2587 of them), world records take the OBJ value (plus 0x200 for gamething links), and the other stamps are 0x1a0 and 0x100 (detail_record_build, mech parts), 0x50 (destructibles and later wtboPartMode parts) and 0x20 (the XPLO chunk, on explosion geometry whose family is 0). READERS: projectile_update's impact dispatch gives an object with 0x400 and no 0x100/0x200/family 0x50 impact flag 0x02, the 'building or vehicle' effect variant, and calls no damage function, so a round striking projectile geometry does nothing to it; polygon_resolve_colour's wireframe view colours it 0xb; debug_command_execute (formerly target_select_section) has a debug key toggling it in textureOffTypeMask. Whether in-flight rounds are on the world chain, where world_raycast (which does not filter on type) could hit them, is NOT established: the launch path's scene calls pass registers the decompiler loses. (This used to list 0x400 as not established.) The game's own name for the class is GS: TOGGLE_GS_TEXT_MAPS is the command that toggles 0x400 in textureOffTypeMask (see commandNames); what the letters stand for is not established. BIT 0x800 is TERRAIN - LANDFORM meshes. Two independent sources. The game's command TOGGLE_TERRAIN_TEXT_MAPS is the one that toggles 0x800 (see textureOffTypeMask), beside TOGGLE_GP_ for 0x100 and TOGGLE_GT_ for 0x200, the mech and gamething classes - GT matching the known gamething class is what confirms the command-to-bit mapping. And in the data the bit is carried by 2587 of the 12182 OBJ placements (2381 as 0x0800, 206 as 0x08c0), all world-record definitions, 2553 of them objectClass 5, and nearly all at height 0: their meshes are T_ACRTR*/T_ACRTZ* craters (1010), T_ARLL* and T_ARHI* rolling land and hills (934), TLADUN* dunes (200), TLBMESA* mesas, TLAMTN* mountains and the like - relief, which fits altTypeLetters' letter r. They are placed singly, not on a grid, so they are features on the ground rather than tiles of it. No code tests the bit directly; its only effect is through textureOffTypeMask. STILL NOT ESTABLISHED: bits 0-3. THE FAMILIES IN THE DATA. The OBJ chunk's dword at +0x34 is this word (project_obj_exec: obj->type = chunk+0x34; +0xc is the objectClass, 0..7 else 4, and +0x32 the load flags). Over all 12182 OBJ chunks in MW2.PRJ, with the POLY mesh names at +0x38: 0x00 x8995 ordinary scenery and props; 0x10 x73 fire and smoke (FIR*, SMO*); 0x30 x153 one mesh per clan colour (AQUASCR1, BRONSCR1, CYANSCR1...); 0x60 x28 jump-jet flames (JET0_*); 0x70 x1763 almost all 'DUMMY', null attachment objects; 0x90 x6 (TL1MARDM, TL1TANA, TL1PDSTL, TL1SIDWK); 0xa0 x19 the mech HEADS (KF5_HEAD, BM5_HEAD, DW5_HEAD...); 0xb0 x158 targets, bridges and buildings (S_1TRGTA, S_ABRDG*, S_BINDPB...); 0xc0 x987 'LIGHT' and the *SPRS* meshes. That lines up with the code that masks 0xf0: 0x10 and 0x60, fire, smoke and jet flame, are the families geom_luma turns to face the camera; 0x70 dummies are taken off the world chain and never freed; 0xa0 is what detail_record_build stamps as 0x1a0 over a mech's part tree, and what object_cull_main_view skips while the flag at 0x96ef4 is set - so that flag hides mech heads, presumably the player's own cockpit shell (the flag's writer was not traced); 0xc0 lights and *SPRS* meshes are what scenery_c0_set_visible (formerly terrain_sub_01fbf0) takes off and puts back on the world lists for two UI callbacks, i.e. an optional scenery-detail class. The meanings are read from the mesh names, not from any name table; 0x30 and 0x90 have no consumer read. CORRECTION: 0x90 has one. vfx_video_sub_0103c0 takes the FIRST family-0x90 object on the world chain as backdropNode and the first family-0xa0 one as cockpitHeadNode; see those labels.
fields.listPrev: back link of the parent/child list. The FIRST element's listPrev points at the sentinel rather than being null, which is why object_unlink can walk backwards without a null check. object_link writes it; object_unlink is the matching remove.
fields.listNext: forward link of the same list. A sentinel's listNext is the list head - that is where object_link reads and writes when it pushes to the front, and where the three pending-free lists live.
fields.worldPrev: back link of the world chain, a membership separate from the parent/child list. world_find_highest_hit walks this chain and object_remove_from_world takes an object out of it without freeing it.
