fields.worldNext: forward link of the world chain. worldRootNode's own worldNext is the chain head, which is the global labelled worldChainHead - the same four bytes, reached as an absolute address.
fields.index: the object's slot in whatever table its type class names. projectile_update reads it as a mechTable slot when type carries bit 0x100 and as a destructibles slot when the family nibble is 0x50, and mech_has_line_of_fire compares it against the low byte of a target handle - the half of a handle that is the index. object_create zeroes it.
fields.hitLocation: which mech section this piece of a mech's geometry belongs to: the 1-based location mech_apply_damage takes (sections[loc - 1]). TWO CONSUMERS AGREE. projectile_update, on a mech hit, passes the struck object's hitLocation as mech_apply_damage's location, ORed with 0x8000 when the shot's direction of travel is within 90 degrees of the mech's heading - a hit from behind. mech_apply_damage then takes the second armour value for locations 2, 3 and 4 (the torsos, the ones with rear armour), and for location 3 also re-rolls among 2, 3 and 4 at random. projectile_update also raises an extra impact flag for the player when it is 1..4. mech_detach_section_geometry(node, section) walks a mech's node tree and hands every node whose object has this value to the destructibles system - that is how a destroyed limb comes off. WRITER: detail_record_build copies DetailRecord.location in through object_set_hit_location, a one-instruction setter of this half-word, and that comes from the OBJL chunk, whose keyword is objloc. object_create zeroes it, so non-mech scenery carries 0.
fields.node: the scene node carrying this object's geometry. object_set_node (formerly geom_luma_sub_038990) sets it, and the billboard pass reads it out and turns it to face the camera for the two type families it selects. object_create zeroes it, so an object exists before its node does.
fields.meshList: head of the object's MESH LIST: WTBO mesh blocks linked through their +0xc, sorted ascending by their first dword. RENAMED from ownedList, and retyped from WorldObject *, which was wrong. The old note said only that object_free walks the list through each entry's +0xc and frees it, and that what the entries hold was not established. object_add_mesh settles it. It is the only code that inserts into the list, and each block it allocates is 0x18 bytes of header, then vertexCount * 0x2c of vertices, polygonCount * 0x24 of polygons, then extra bytes. The header stores the polygon table offset at +8, and the block is linked into this list in key order. object_build_ground_quadtree and the walkmesh_* methods read the head as a mesh: vertex count at +4, polygon count at +6, polygon table at +8, vertices from +0x18. THE SORT KEY at mesh +0 IS THE LEVEL-OF-DETAIL SWITCH DISTANCE: object_draw_lod_mesh walks this list each frame and keeps the last mesh whose key * Viewer.lodScale is within the object's view depth, so the list runs from the finest mesh (smallest key) to the coarsest. The loader takes the key from a numeric suffix on the mesh name, and in MW2.PRJ a high-detail mesh is typically NAME_1 and its low-detail partner NAME_15000 (or 25000, 35000...), with fewer polygons. object_create's first mesh has key 0 until object_set_mesh_key sets it
fields.currentMesh: the mesh block object_add_mesh allocated LAST. It sets this on every call, whatever the block's place in the key-sorted meshList. object_set_mesh_key writes the key through it, and objectClass 2's methods (downface_point_inside, mesh_raycast_all) read their polygons from it rather than from meshList. object_create zeroes it alongside meshList.
fields.objectClass: the object's class, straight out of the mission data - the cls field of an OBJ record in the area file. object_set_class is the only writer, and the poly handler is the only caller, passing the value it read from the chunk after bounding it to 0..7. It decides world-chain membership, and the setter enforces that rather than leaving it to callers: 4 means NOT a world-chain member, so object_set_class calls object_remove_from_world for 4 and object_add_to_world for everything else. object_link honours the same rule from the other side by setting flags bit 0x0800 when it sees 4, and a cleanup sweep in vfx_video removes any object it finds carrying 4. object_create writes 4 before anything else, so off-chain is the state an object is born in. 5 is the other value with a known consequence: the poly handler calls object_build_ground_quadtree (formerly project_entry_sub_01cf10) on it, one of the two functions that allocate quadtrees. The rest are real but unread - the shipped missions use 0, 1, 4, 5, 6 and 7 across 12182 OBJ records counted out of MW2.PRJ, 5 being much the commonest.
fields.localX: the point object_update_world_pos transforms into posX, posY and posZ. It is read as a POINT and not as anything else: that function dots the triple against the three rows of the node's world matrix and adds the matrix's translation, which is p' = M p + T and nothing else. CAVEAT WORTH KEEPING: the only writer found so far is object_create, which zeroes all three. If nothing else ever writes them the transform reduces to the node's own translation, and calling this a pivot would be reading more into it than the code shows. Named for the role its one consumer gives it; what sets a non-zero value, if anything does, has not been found.
fields.posX: the object's world position. object_get_pos_radius hands out this triple as x, y and z, and gamethings_near_point differences them against the point it is querying from - so they are coordinates in the same space as everything else, not local offsets. object_create zeroes all three in one group.
fields.radius: the object's bounding radius, and the field object_get_pos_radius RETURNS beside the position. Two independent uses in one line of gamethings_near_point fix it: the blast query compares its octagonal distance against the querying object's radius plus the candidate's own radius, the first read straight off this field and the second through the getter. A sphere-overlap test with a radius from each side is not something two unrelated fields would spell.
fields.bounds: six ints - a min and a max for each axis - or null. ray_hit_object_box reads it as piVar1[0..5] and feeds consecutive pairs to ray_slab_intersect alongside Ray.startX/unitX, then Y, then Z, which is what fixes both the count and the pairing. Bailing out when it is null is the first thing that function does after refreshing the object.
fields.transformVersion: a counter bumped every time the object's world position is recomputed: object_update_world_pos ends with transformVersion += 1. Each mesh block keeps the value it was last transformed at in its +0x10, and object_draw_lod_mesh and object_compute_bounds re-run object_refresh_mesh whenever the two differ. So it is a dirty stamp, and a mesh's world vertices are only recomputed after the object has moved. object_create zeroes it.

fields.name: the formation's name, and the reason the first 16 bytes were padding: group_set_formation_by_name strcmps its argument against offset 0 of each formationPresets row, so a row begins with a NUL-terminated name and the three int[5] arrays start at 0x10. The names come from the project file - 'formation' is one of the projectKeywords - which is also why formationPresets is all zeroes in the image.
fields.slotX: x position for each star slot
fields.slotZ: z position for each star slot

fields.id: which kind of projectile this pool entry is, matched against WeaponType.projectileKind when a weapon looks for a free one. Reset to -1, so -1 is the empty value. id 7 is Gauss, and projectile_update tests for it by name. WHO STOCKS THE POOL: the BTHG chunk (keyword booyowthing), in project_chunk_exec. Its short at +8 is a project object id, passed through project_mangle_id and project_object_find, and its short at +0xa is the kind. For slot projectileSlotFill, if the slot has no node yet and the object resolves to one, it stores id = kind and node = that object's node, zeroes motionHeld, takes the node out of the world, and stamps its subtree with type 0x400. The counter advances whether or not the slot was filled, and slots stop at 0xaf. IN MW2.PRJ exactly two BWD resources carry BTHG chunks, MW2_SHT1 and MW2_SHT2, 159 each. Walked with dump_objectives' chunk walker over every BWD, the two have the same kind sequence and different object ids. 59 scene files INCL one of them, 56 MW2_SHT1 and 3 MW2_SHT2. So every mission stocks 159 of the 175 slots, and the count per kind is: 0: 11, 1: 11, 2: 11, 3: 32, 4: 48, 5: 32, 6: 8, 7: 6. mech_weapon_fire launches a round only if a slot of the weapon's kind is inactive, so THESE ARE THE CAPS ON ROUNDS IN FLIGHT, shared by every mech. For example, 48 LRM or Streak missiles (kind 4), and 6 Gauss slugs. No slot has kind 22, the NUKE's projectileKind, so the nuke never launches a pool projectile; its blast is driven by the nukeBlast globals instead.
fields.effectIndex: the effectTypes index this projectile detonates into, copied from WeaponType.impactEffect when the shot is created. It and impactFlags are one 32-bit word: projectile_destroy reads all four bytes at +0x04 and hands them to effect_spawn, which takes the low byte as the index and the rest as variant flags.
fields.impactFlags: written only by projectile_update, one bit per branch of its impact resolution, so each bit records a classification of what was hit. Bit 6 (0x40) is the one with unambiguous evidence: set when the owner is the player. Bit 4 (0x10) is set when id == 7. Bits 0, 1 and 2 are chosen by a surface word tested against 0x100, 0x200 and 0x400. CORRECTION: this used to end 'nothing in the decompiled game code ever reads this, so the consumer is elsewhere'. The consumer is effect_spawn. This byte is the second byte of the effect code at +0x04, so these bits arrive there as 0x100, 0x200, 0x400, 0x1000, 0x2000 and 0x4000 - and those are exactly the six bits effect_spawn switches on to pick a variant of the impact effect. THE BITS, from projectile_update's impact branch (sim_objects.c, the block that dispatches on the struck WorldObject.type), each set by exactly one test. It starts as byte 1 of WeaponType.impactEffect, 0 for every weapon, then ORs in: 0x01 (code 0x100) the round hit a MECH - class bit 0x100, the branch that calls mech_apply_damage; 0x10 (0x1000) ALSO that the projectile's id is 7, Gauss; 0x40 (0x4000) ALSO that the mech is the player's; 0x20 (0x2000) ALSO that the player's mech was hit in location 1..4 - head, right, centre or left torso, not an arm or leg; 0x02 (0x200) the round hit a GAMETHING (class 0x200, the gamething_apply_damage branch) or an object whose type has bit 0x400, which the BTHG chunk stamps on pooled projectile geometry; 0x04 (0x400) the round hit the GROUND - the world_ground_height_near test when nothing else was struck - or an object with none of those class bits, plain scenery. A destructible (family 0x50) sets nothing. So in effect_spawn +0x400 is 'hit terrain or scenery' (lasers and machine guns then ricochet, row 9), +0x200 'hit a building or vehicle', +0x100 'hit a mech', and +0x2000 'hit the player in the torso or head', which is how a missile hit on the player's cockpit gets row 0x11 and its MIS2HEAD sound. +0x4000 picks no variant at all: effect_spawn tests it once, at 0x5109f, into a local whose only reader (0x51593) makes the impact sound's last sound_play_at argument 0 instead of 1 - as a cameraMode other than 0 also does; what that argument does is NOT established. REFINES the earlier text, which had bits 0..2 as 'chosen by a surface word tested against 0x100, 0x200 and 0x400' and 0x10 as 'id == 7' without saying what either meant.
fields.effectHigh: the top half of the effect dword at +4, copied with effectIndex and impactFlags from bytes 2 and 3 of WeaponType.impactEffect when mech_weapon_fire launches the round. projectile_clear sets it to 0xffff. It is NEVER READ: projectile_destroy hands the whole dword at +4 to effect_spawn, which masks the code with 0xff and 0xff00 only (checked in its disassembly). Those two bytes are 0 for every weapon in the table except the flamer's -1, and the flamer fires no projectile. So this is carried padding, named for its position
fields.velX: VELOCITY, not position. RENAMED from x (and +0x0c/+0x10 from y/z), noted as 'integrated by vx * tickDelta' - which was true, and is exactly what velocity does. A projectile's position lives in its scene node: projectile_update starts from scene_node_get_world_pos(node), computes new position = node position + (velX + accelX*dt/2) * dt and new velocity = velX + accelX*dt, writes the position with scene_node_set_origin and the velocity back here. mech_weapon_fire confirms it from the other side, setting these to projectileSpeed times a unit aim vector; and the two other readers only make sense for a velocity - fixed_atan2(velX, velZ) is the direction of travel projectile_update compares with the struck mech's heading, and view_shake_impulse is handed the vector
fields.accelX: ACCELERATION. RENAMED from vx (and +0x18/+0x1c from vy/vz), described as 'velocity'. It is what projectile_update adds to velX each tick, with the half-step term that makes the position update second order. mech_weapon_fire sets accelX = accelZ = 0 and accelY = -gravity * WeaponType.gravityScale - so this is the drop, and it is zero for everything but the few weapons with gravityScale 1
fields.age: accumulates tickDelta every frame, in projectiles_update_all, before the step. mech_weapon_fire starts it at the firing weapon's stateTick - the burst clock from the previous tick, about shotGap - tickDelta - not at 0, and takes the same amount off timeLeft. Its only reader is projectile_update's age > 0 guard on homing. See projectile_update, THE AGED LAUNCH
fields.timeLeft: decremented by tickDelta every frame. Starts at WeaponType.flightTime minus the age the round is launched with; when it is below 1 on a step with no hit, projectile_update destroys the round with no effect
fields.node: its node in the scene tree
fields.targetIndex: index half of the handle this projectile is homing on. CORRECTION: this pair was named ownerIndex and ownerType, described as the firing object's handle. It is the TARGET, not the shooter, and the shooter was never here - attackerMechIndex at +0x40 has always held that and is documented as the mech credited with the shot. Three things settle it. The weapon only fills lockIndex and lockType, which cockpit copies straight into this pair, when the weapon type is guided AND the mech has a lock; otherwise it writes 0 to both. An unguided shot still has an owner, so a field that is zero for unguided shots is not one. projectile_update resolves the pair to a world object and uses it as the thing to steer at. And the per-tick correction is gated on targetType being non-zero and the projectile having aged, then reads that entity's posX and turns the projectile toward it - homing, which only makes sense against a target.
fields.targetType: type half of the homing handle: 0x200 means mechTable, 0x400 means gameThings, 0 means unguided. See targetIndex for why this is not the owner.
fields.active: the update skips the slot when this is zero or node is null. BIT 0x8000 is a PROXIMITY HIT, set by projectile_home when a homing round comes within 0x65 (about 1 m) of its target: while it is set, projectile_update skips world_raycast and takes the target's own object as the thing hit, at the position the projectile had at the start of that tick. The low bits hold 1 for an active round. projectile_clear zeroes the whole dword
fields.motionHeld: while non-zero, projectiles_update_all still ages the round and counts timeLeft down, but does not call projectile_update, so it neither moves, homes nor hits anything. Its only reader is that test. Every writer found stores 0: mech_weapon_fire at launch, projectile_clear, and project_chunk_exec's BTHG chunk, which gives projectiles[] slots their id and scene node from project objects, one slot per chunk. A scan of every function for the absolute address 0x15397c found only the BTHG store, but register-based stores could not be ruled out that way. So NO WRITER OF A NON-ZERO VALUE IS KNOWN, and in the code read so far the hold never engages. The name says what the reader does with it, not who uses it
fields.attackerMechIndex: the mech credited with the shot. Copied from the firing mech's own index, handed to ai_log_attack as the attacker half of 'Mech %2d has attacked mech %2d', and stashed in killCreditMech before a gamething dies so gamething_destroy knows whether the player scored it. THIS is the shooter. The pair at +0x30 and +0x34 was once called ownerIndex and ownerType and this note said it was distinct from them because the firing code took it from a different object - true, but it read as though the owner lived in both places. It does not: that pair is targetIndex and targetType, the homing handle, and the shooter is only ever here.
fields.damage: copied from WeaponType.damage when the shot is created. Against a mech it is shifted left 0x10 and handed to mech_apply_damage; against a gamething it is what gamething_apply_damage subtracts from GameThing.hitPoints.
fields.heatOnHit: heat dealt to a struck mech: mech_weapon_fire copies WeaponType.heatOnHit here, and projectile_update adds it to the target's MechLoadout.heatThisTick just before mech_apply_damage
fields.missileCam: 1 while the missile camera follows this projectile. Only missile_cam_follow_last sets it, on the player's last missile. While it is set, every projectile_update step writes the projectile's position and heading into missileCamPose and sets missileCamProjectile to the slot. projectile_destroy drops the follow (missileCamProjectile = -1) when a flagged projectile dies, and projectile_clear zeroes it

fields.inUse: 1 from sound_seq_queue_message until the line is dropped or finished
fields.soundId: the first record's SNDS id (the prefix when there are two)
fields.bodySoundId: the second record's SNDS id, played after the first by sound_sample_eos's chaining
fields.buffer: the first record's field 2: a caller's malloc'd sound played instead of a resource, freed when the line is dropped (the mission-result lines)
fields.bodyBuffer: the second record's field 2 - always 0, since sound_seq_queue_message drops a second record that has one; freed like buffer
fields.endTick: 0 while the line plays as sound; simTick + 0x71c when voice_line_start posted it as text
fields.priority: the queue is kept in descending order of it; the caller's, or soundSettings[soundId]'s
fields.text: first text, a separator, second text and a terminator, bounded at 0x33 bytes
fields.next: the next line in the queue

fields.inUse: set to 1 on creation and only ever tested against zero, so this is an allocated flag rather than a type. It was called 'kind' until the consumers were checked. NAVP loads it from the short at chunk +0x18 rather than writing 1; NAVO writes 1.
fields.followNode: a scene node the entry is pinned to, or null for a fixed point. Both readers - ai_validate_tracked, which then fills MechEntity.targetX/Y/Z from the entry, and vfx_video_sub_011f60 - test it first and, when set, take x/y/z from scene_node_get_world_pos on it instead of the stored values; the AI one writes the fresh position back into x/y/z. NAVO sets it when its object id resolves through project_object_find rather than world_record_find; NAVP and tracked_object_create set 0.
fields.targetHandle: a (type << 8) | index handle; created as mechIndex | 0x200. NAVP loads it from the short at chunk +0x1c; NAVO writes 0. ai_validate_tracked only consults it when flags bit 0 is set, and then refuses any mech whose index | 0x200 is not this - so a navpoint can be private to one mech
fields.groupId: copied from the target mech's groupId. NAVP loads it from the short at chunk +0x1e. ai_validate_tracked refuses a mech of any other group, and vfx_video_sub_011f60 only walks entries whose groupId is playerGroupIndex - so every navpoint belongs to one group
fields.range: the object's effective radius. Every read compares it against MechEntity.targetDistance; it is never decremented and never compared against simTick or tickDelta. One creator sets 3000, another takes it from a per-type table. NOTE: this was first called 'lifetime' purely because 3000 looked like a timer in the creator - an initialiser told me the value, not the meaning. From the mission file: NAVP stores the unsigned short at chunk +0x20 multiplied by 100, NAVO the signed short at +0xc as-is.
fields.heading: the object's facing. Written in only ONE of the two branches that build a TrackedObject - the scene-node branch, from the middle output of scene_node_get_world_euler, which is the yaw; the world_object_get_pos branch leaves it alone. Its one reader passes it as the heading argument of star_place_formation, which writes it into MechEntity.heading, so writer and reader agree. NOTE: this was left unnamed on a previous pass, correctly on the evidence then - the euler component order was recorded as unestablished, and one consumer plus an unknown axis order is not enough. It is established now; see scene_node_get_world_euler. CORRECTION to 'only ONE of the two branches': there are three writers, not two. The NAVP chunk writes it straight from chunk +0x14, alongside its fixed x/y/z; the two branches described above are both NAVO's
fields.x: position, from the caller. NAVP takes x/y/z from chunk +8/+0xc/+0x10 and runs them through block_transform_point first, so a navpoint written inside a BLK is in that block's frame; NAVO takes them from world_object_get_pos. Overwritten from followNode whenever that is set
fields.y: the HEIGHT, a real coordinate: ai_validate_tracked differences it against the mech's posY for vec_to_range_bearing, and ai_group_sub_028ed0 and ai_ring_target_with_navpoints use it as y too. BUT TWO CREATORS PUT A HEADING HERE: the star-follow waypoint (0x235e0, via star_get_slot_target) and point_around_target's waypoints (via ai_goto_point_near_target). Both are confirmed in the disassembly. For those, bearing and horizontal distance are unaffected but slant range and elevation are wrong; see point_around_target
fields.flags: initialised to 0x401. Bit 0 marks a TEMPORARY, mech-owned waypoint: it is what mech_reclaim_waypoints (formerly mech_reclaim_waypoints (formerly ai_check_incoming)) requires before deleting an entry whose targetHandle is the mech, and what tracked_object_remove requires before removing anything - so entries without it (NAVO writes 0) can never be removed that way. bit 0x20 marks that a mech has already reacted to it. NAVP loads the word at chunk +0x1a; NAVO writes 0. Bit 0 also makes targetHandle binding (ai_validate_tracked) and hides the entry from vfx_video_sub_011f60; bit 0x40 is required when ai_validate_tracked is called with mode bit 0x10000. Conversely, with mode bit 0x100 an entry WITHOUT bit 0 is refused (-6): that is ai_cycle_navpoint's ownWaypointsOnly, which restricts the AI's waypoint stepping to its own temporary entries
fields.seenByGroups: bit per group: set as 1 << (mech->groupId & 0x1f) when a group first notices this object
fields.name: the tracked object's display name. lance_slot_target_name is a handle-to-name resolver: given (type << 8) | index it returns trackedObjects + index * 0x54 + 0x28 for type 1, MechEntity.name for type 2 and GameThing.name for type 4, so this is the tracked table's slot in that set. NAVP copies it from chunk +0x24, 0x15 bytes, and forces a NUL after them.
fields.field_0x3e: 22 bytes to the end of the record, WRITTEN BY NOTHING that has been found. CORRECTION: this was named nameAlt, with a note saying it was loaded by the same strncpy pair as name, 22 bytes further into the project record. That note was carried over from GameThing.nameAlt, where it is true, and it does not hold here. Both TrackedObject creators in the mission VM were read in the disassembly: NAVP (0x4f4d0) copies ONE string, 0x15 bytes from chunk +0x24 into name, and forces a NUL at +0x3d; NAVO (0x4f5d0) copies none. No absolute relocation lands in +0x3e..+0x53 of any trackedObjects entry, no exported code writes a TrackedObject's nameAlt, and the NAVP chunk's own bytes at +0x3a..+0x4f are zero in all 576 chunks of MW2.PRJ. So it is unnamed until a consumer turns up. Anything written while it was called nameAlt about a navpoint's second name was the GameThing fact, not a TrackedObject one

fields.projectileKind: which pre-built projectile this weapon borrows (see Projectile.id for how many of each kind the BTHG chunks stock, which caps rounds in flight). The firing code scans the 175 projectiles for one whose Projectile.id equals this and that is inactive but still has a scene node, so the pool is stocked by kind and a weapon can only fire the kind it names. Kind 7 is the one projectile_update singles out - id == 7 sets the 0x1000 bit of the effect code - and 7 is GAUSS, which is why the Gauss impact takes a different branch of the ballistic effect from every other autocannon.
fields.impactEffect: the effect code the projectile carries to its grave. The firing code copies these four bytes into Projectile +0x04; projectile_update ORs its classification bits into byte 5 of the same word as it resolves the hit; projectile_destroy then hands the whole word to effect_spawn. -1 on the flamer and the nuke, neither of which fires a projectile. The low byte is an effectTypes index: 0/1/2 the three laser sizes, 3 missiles, 5 machine gun and AMS, 6 PPC, 8 NARC, 11 every autocannon and Gauss, 22 the nuke.
fields.muzzleEffects: two effect codes spawned together on the weapon's own node when it fires - the firing code calls effect_spawn_on_mount with [0] then [1]. Both are always in 23..31, which is exactly the range effect_spawn attaches to a mount instead of placing at a world position, and they group by family: 23/24 ballistic, 26/27 missile, 28/29 laser, 30/31 PPC. -1 on the flamer and the nuke. Which of the two is which is NOT established; they differ only in that the second index is one higher.
fields.autoRepeat: non-zero if the weapon keeps firing while the trigger is held. The only reader is the end of a burst in mech_weapons_tick (0x52588..0x525d1), when shotsLeft has reached zero. With this clear, the weapon is left in fireState 2 with no shots, drops to 0 - cooldown - on the next tick and to 1 after reload, and a new burst needs a fresh press, since loadout->flags bit 1 latches the trigger edge. With it set, AND any of weapon_fire or the four fire-group controls held (ControlState +0x25, +0x27..+0x2a), it goes straight to fireState 3 with stateTick = simTick and shotsLeft refilled from shots. fireState 3 returns to 2 once reload has passed with the trigger still down. Set for MGun, the xAC and uAC autocannons, the three lasers, the three pulse lasers, AMS and NUKE; clear for the LRMs, SRMs, streak SRMs, GAUSS, FLAMER, PPC and NARC. CORRECTIONS: the trigger latch is flags value 0x0001 (bit 0), and fireState 3 returns to 2 once reload has passed when the weapon is the SELECTED one or a group-fire control (+0x27..+0x2a) is down - weapon_fire (+0x25) is not tested there, so a released selected weapon can fire one more burst; see mech_weapons_tick
fields.launchesProjectile: mech_weapon_fire only launches a projectile when this is non-zero. It is 1 on every weapon but the flamer, which is 0
fields.guided: set on the four LRMs, the three Streak SRMs and NARC, and clear on the plain SRMs and everything ballistic or energy - which is exactly the set of MW2 weapons that track. ALSO decides which fire an AI target can dodge: weapon_fire_alert_target alerts the mech being shot at only for a guided weapon or the PPC (type 0x15)
fields.shots: projectiles per trigger pull: 20/15/10/5 down the LRMs, 6/4/2 down the SRMs, 2 for every pulse laser and 1 otherwise
fields.ammoPerTon: -1 on the energy weapons. The rest are the tabletop numbers
fields.fireSound: the SNDS resource the weapon plays when a burst starts. weapons_preload_sounds (formerly weapons_snds_handler) preloads every positive one exactly as it preloads effectTypes[].soundId, and the burst loop in mech_weapons_tick plays it on the burst's first shot - through ai_group_sub_0287f0 with a pan chosen by the weapon's section for the player's own mech, and through sound_play_at relative to viewerPosition for everyone else. Zero or less means silent
fields.gravityScale: mech_weapon_fire sets the projectile's accelY to -gravity times this. 1 on the machine gun, the three Streak SRMs, NARC and AMS; 0 on everything else, so every other projectile flies straight
fields.projectileSpeed: 600 for AMS down to 70 for missiles; 0 for the nuke. UNITS: centimetres per 182 Hz tick. mech_weapon_fire sets the projectile's velocity to this times the 16.16 unit aim vector, and projectile_update advances position by (velocity * tickDelta) >> 16 in centimetres - the same integration as mech movement. So m/s = speed * 1.82: LRMs 100 -> 182 m/s, lasers 280 -> 509.6 m/s, AMS 600 -> 1092 m/s
fields.damage: per projectile, so an LRM20 deals shots * damage. The lasers carry their tabletop 8/5/3; the autocannons are scaled up. WHAT A HIT COSTS, from projectile_update's mech branch: mech_apply_damage(loadout, damage << 16, location | rear), so each point is ONE WHOLE ARMOUR POINT off armour that mech_load_config (formerly mech_dump_config) already multiplied by the difficulty armour scale. In chassis-file points a medium laser's 5 therefore costs the player's mech 1.25 at every difficulty (x4 armour) and an enemy 5 at difficulty 0 (x1). The location is the struck part's WorldObject.hitLocation. The REAR flag 0x8000 is set when the target's heading and the projectile's direction of travel, fixed_atan2(velX, velZ), are within 0x5a0000 - 90 degrees - of each other: a shot travelling the way the target faces hits its back, and mech_apply_damage then uses rear armour on the torsos. heatOnHit is added to the TARGET's heatThisTick in the same branch
fields.heat: PER SHOT: the burst loop in mech_weapons_tick adds it to heatThisTick once for every round fired, so a volley costs shots * heat - the LRM20's 0.6 is 12 percent a volley, a PPC's 12.5 is 12.5. 16.16 fixed point on the same 0..100 scale as heatLevel. The firing code in cockpit adds it to heatThisTick and mech_heat_update integrates that into heatLevel; the AI separately adds it to heatLevel as a prediction, to decide whether the shot would push past 65. PPC is the hottest at 12.5; the machine gun and AMS generate none
fields.heatOnHit: heat, in the same 16.16 units as heat, added to the mech a projectile hits - copied to Projectile.heatOnHit at launch. Non-zero on the PPC alone, at 229376 = 3.5
fields.minRange: 7500 on the four LRMs, 25 on the Streaks, 1000 on the flamer, zero everywhere else. Centimetres, like maxRange: the LRMs will not fire inside 75 m
fields.maxRange: same units as MechEntity.targetDistance. Gauss reaches furthest of the real weapons at 182000. CENTIMETRES: flightTime is maxRange / projectileSpeed in 22 of the 31 rows, and speed is established as cm per tick, so this is the distance a round covers before it expires - 1820 m for the Gauss rifle, 1001 m for the LRMs, 509.6 m for the medium laser (one second of flight)
fields.reload: ticks between shots. Every Ultra autocannon is exactly half its LB-X counterpart. ai_decide_fire (formerly ai_aim_torso) feeds it to random_range divided by 0x5b, so the AI's rate of fire is this jittered rather than exact
fields.shotGap: 182 Hz ticks between the shots of one burst. mech_weapons_tick starts from stateTick + tickDelta, fires while that is at least shotGap and shotsLeft remains, and subtracts shotGap per shot - so a burst of `shots` rounds takes about shots * shotGap ticks, and a long frame can fire several at once. The shipped values are 5..182: 11 for the LRM20 and machine gun, 60 for the three standard lasers, 182 (one second) for the flamer and nuke
fields.flightTime: how long a projectile lives: mech_weapon_fire sets Projectile.timeLeft from it and projectile_update destroys the shot when that runs out. Mostly it is not an independent number: in 22 of the 31 rows it is exactly maxRange / projectileSpeed truncated (MLASER 50960/280 = 182, LRM20 100100/100 = 1001) and in four more it is within one (GAUSS, xAC10, uAC5, uAC20), so a shot normally expires at about its maximum range - which also makes projectileSpeed a distance per unit of timeLeft. The exceptions are real, not rounding: SRM2 has 709, the figure the other SRMs get from speed 70, although its own speed is 100; NARC has 1456 against 2500; AMS 273 against 16; the flamer launches nothing; the nuke has speed 0. CORRECTION to 'a shot normally expires at about its maximum range': a round starts with timeLeft = flightTime - the firing weapon's stateTick, about shotGap - tickDelta, so it expires that much sooner - the medium laser at about 65 percent of its range and the small laser at 31. See projectile_update, THE AGED LAUNCH
fields.name: eight bytes, not terminated when full

fields.slotState: -1 means no weapon in this slot. Three values, from their writers: mech_std_create_loadout resets all ten slots to -1 (with type and fireState), mech_load_config (formerly mech_dump_config) writes 1 for each weapon it fills in, and mech_damage_slot writes 0 - beside fireState = -1 - when the weapon is destroyed by a critical hit or when its ammo bin cooking off leaves it with none. The SELECTION consumers only test for -1: weapon_cycle_next and mech_weapons_tick treat a -1 in the next slot as the end of the list and wrap to slot 0, and the three fire-group selectors refuse a -1 slot. 0 as DESTROYED has a consumer too: when a critical lands on a weapon slot of the player's mech, mech_damage_slot plays the weapon-type callout (0x16..0x1a, chosen by slotCode / 100) only while slotState is still non-zero, then sets it to 0 - so a weapon is announced lost once. Selection keeps a destroyed weapon out through its fireState of -1, not through this field
fields.type: printed as 'weapon %d: type %d', and an index into weaponTypes - mech_config derives it as slotCode / 100.
fields.fireState: the weapon's firing state machine, driven by the cockpit tick. 0 is cooling down, and becomes 1 once simTick - stateTick reaches the weapon type's reload. 1 is ready. 2 is mid-burst: it counts shotsLeft down and drops to 0 when they run out, stamping stateTick to start the cooldown. 3 is the hold after a burst, which goes to 2 if the trigger is still down or this is the selected weapon, and to 1 otherwise. -1 is terminal and means out of ammo: the firing path writes it the moment ammo reaches exactly 0, and mech_has_no_usable_weapon treats any slot that is not -1 as still able to fire. CORRECTION. This field was named usable earlier in this same session, described as 1 or -1 only, on the strength of mech_config writing 1 and the ammo path writing -1. That was a partial view: mech_weapon_fire (formerly cockpit_sub_052620)'s weapon argument was still untyped, so its writes of 0, 2 and 3 were invisible as bare +8 offsets. Typing that parameter exposed them. The old name was not merely narrow, it was the wrong shape - a boolean where the code has four states plus a terminal one. CORRECTIONS from mech_weapons_tick read end to end (see its note for the full machine): the first round of a burst waits shotGap ticks after the arming; state 3 goes to 2 when this is the SELECTED weapon or a GROUP-fire control is held - the weapon_fire trigger itself is not tested - and to 1 otherwise; and -1 is terminal because that function compares fireState unsigned, so it matches no state. The 1 -> 2 arming is done by mech_weapons_tick for the selected weapon and by player_fire_group for a group.
fields.fireGroup: which of the three fire groups the weapon belongs to, 0..2. The game's own control names fix it: mech_weapons_tick answers weapon_fire_group_1 with weapon_select_group(loadout, 0), _2 with 1 and _3 with 2, then fires. weapon_select_next_in_group steps selectedWeapon to the next usable weapon whose fireGroup equals the current one's, and weapon_select_next_group searches (fireGroup + 1) % 10 onward for the first group that has any. Three writers: mech_load_config (formerly mech_dump_config) starts every weapon in group 0; weapon_set_fire_group ignores values outside 0..2; and player_weapon_set_fire_group stores its argument unchecked, but its only caller passes 0, 1 or 2 for option commands 0x8e, 0x8f and 0x90
fields.stateTick: the simTick that fireState last changed at, and the only thing the reload timer measures from: both the 0 -> 1 and the 3 -> 2 transitions test simTick - stateTick against the weapon type's reload. Stamped when a burst ends and zeroed when a transition consumes it.
fields.lockIndex: index half of the target lock this weapon fired with, captured from MechEntity.targetHandle at the moment the trigger arms the burst and copied into Projectile.targetIndex when the round launches. The capture is conditional and that is what gives the field its meaning: the weapons module writes it only when the weapon type is guided and the mech's specialFlags carry 0x80, and writes 0 to this and lockType otherwise. So a guided weapon fired without a lock, and every unguided weapon, launches with 0 here. mech_config does not initialise either field - only the trigger path ever writes them.
fields.lockType: type half of the same handle, masked with 0xf00 where lockIndex takes 0xff - the split MechEntity.targetHandle uses everywhere.
fields.ammo: printed as 'ammo = %ld'. An ammo explosion subtracts the bin's remaining rounds from this, and reaching exactly zero disables the weapon.
fields.shotsLeft: rounds remaining in the current burst. Loaded from the weapon type's shots whenever a burst is armed - the cockpit tick does it going to state 3, the player trigger path in weapons does it going from 1 to 2 - counted down while in state 2, and when it falls below 1 the weapon drops to state 0 and starts cooling. Compared against the type's shots to recognise the first shot of a burst. CORRECTION: the single-weapon arming (1 -> 2) is in mech_weapons_tick, not in the weapons module; the weapons module's player_fire_group arms groups.
fields.sectionIndex: which of the eight locations carries it; 6 and 7 are remapped to 1 and 3. IT IS 0-BASED - sections[sectionIndex], i.e. location number - 1 - on three consumers: mech_load_config (formerly mech_dump_config)'s slot search assigns the loop index over sections[0..7] directly, so the 6 -> 1 and 7 -> 3 remap sends leg-mounted weapons to the side torsos; the burst code turns it into a mount-node index as sectionIndex + 1; and loadout_regroup_weapons splits the weapons into {5, 3, 7} and {4, 1, 6}, which read 0-based are {location 6 arm, 4 side torso, 8 leg} and {location 5 arm, 2 side torso, 7 leg} - the two SIDES of the mech, matching mech_destroy_section's 2-carries-5 and 4-carries-6. So locations 2, 5, 7 are one side and 4, 6, 8 the other. WHICH SIDE IS LEFT IS STILL NOT ESTABLISHED, and the obvious source does not settle it. The player's weapon sound is panned by a jump table on sectionIndex (0x52507..0x52528) - 2 and 5 to 0x4f, 4 and 6 to 0x2f, 3 explicitly to the 0x40 centre - and that table only makes physical sense read as LOCATION numbers (3 the centre torso). Applied to the 0-based value the game actually stores, it pans centre-torso weapons right and side-torso weapons centre. It looks like a shipped bug, and a table that disagrees with its own input cannot be trusted to say which side is left. The location callouts in damageCallouts ('left leg' .. 'head') would settle it, but no code references entries 13..21. RESOLVED by debug_command_execute (formerly target_select_section), which names every location in the game's own words: 'Head Selected' stores 1 in testDamageLocation, 'Right Torso' 2, 'Center Torso' 3, 'Left Torso' 4, 'Right Arm' 5, 'Left Arm' 6, 'Right Leg' 7, 'Left Leg' 8; and mech_std_tick_ai passes that value straight to mech_damage_slot as its 1-based location. So the side of 2, 5 and 7 is the RIGHT side and 4, 6 and 8 the LEFT - which also confirms the pan table's intent, 2 and 5 panned right, 0x4f of Miles' 0..127
fields.slotCode: the raw MechSection.slots entry this weapon was built from. mech_damage_slot matches on it to find which weapon a damaged slot belongs to.
fields.numBins: how many ammo bins feed this weapon. mech_config increments it once per bin whose slotCode matches the weapon, in the same step that fills the bin and adds its rounds to this weapon's ammo total. The firing path reads it back as the end stop: when the current bin runs out it steps binCursor on and, if that would reach numBins, steps it straight back again rather than walking off the end. The same loop writes a parallel array of global bin indices starting at +0x34, one int per bin. THAT ARRAY HAS NO READER anywhere in the game code, so it is left unnamed; note only that it would collide with binCursor beyond eleven entries.
fields.binIndices: indices into MechLoadout.ammo of the bins feeding this weapon, numBins of them. mech_load_config (formerly mech_dump_config) appends each bin's index as it attaches it. The consumer is loadout_regroup_weapons: when it moves a weapon to a new position in the array, it walks this list and rewrites each listed bin's MechAmmoBin.weaponIndex to the new position. Ten ints end exactly at +0x5c, where originalIndex starts
fields.originalIndex: the weapon's slot in chassis order, 0..9. loadout_regroup_weapons stamps weapons[i].originalIndex = i and THEN reorders the array, so this is the only record of where a weapon started. Its consumer is the network code: whenever the player's weapon fires, mech_weapons_tick sets byte originalIndex of the ten-byte table at 0x1593f0, and netplay_build_state (formerly netplay_sub_044b70) packs those flags into bits 5..14 of the state packet and clears them. So a remote machine is told which weapon fired in chassis order, regardless of the local reordering. The loadout reset writes 0 before the stamp
fields.binCursor: which of this weapon's bins is currently feeding it, counted from 0. The cockpit firing path is the only thing that moves it: after decrementing ammo it reads the current bin's rounds, and when those are already 0 it advances this and the bin pointer together - bin by the 0x14 stride, this by one - unless doing so would reach numBins, in which case it undoes the increment and leaves both where they were.
fields.bin: the bin currently feeding this weapon. mech_config points it at the start of MechLoadout.ammo when the loadout is built, and the firing path walks it forward by one MechAmmoBin as each bin empties. Typed from its use rather than its assignment: the firing path reads +2 off it as a short and decrements it, and +2 is MechAmmoBin.rounds. The 0x14 it advances by is that struct's stride, which MechLoadout.ammo already records.

fields.pane: where the menu is drawn: 16.16 fractions of the screen in the module, pixels after menu_layout
fields.flags: bit 0 the menu takes keys (menu_poll_key; input_sub_048c50/_048c60 around it); bit 1 no frame during a map transition; bit 2 the pane framed and the title ruled across the pane; bit 3 the exit item not moved to the last row; bit 4 the back pane aligned to the pane's left; bit 5 the pane wiped to 0 each frame
fields.stack: 8 menu pointers, the open menu and those under it
fields.depth: menus on the stack; the context closes at 0
fields.backShpId: SHP id (plus assetVariant) drawn at the back pane's origin each frame; -1 none
fields.backPane: the background shape's pane, sized to the shape by menu_layout
fields.cursorShpId: SHP id drawn at the cursor point of the selected item; -1 none
fields.enterSound: SNDS played entering a submenu; -1 none
fields.moveSound: SNDS played when the selection moves; -1 none
fields.fontId: FONT id (plus assetVariant) of every text
fields.font: loaded by menu_load_art; no font draws nothing
fields.ink: its low byte goes to the text colour table's ink (0xa4dd2) for the title and items
fields.selectedInk: the ink of the selected item
fields.rows: rows the pane is divided into: the row step is 1 / (rows + 2)
fields.rowX: the x of the row step point, 0
fields.titleX: the title point, a fraction of the pane in the module
fields.titleY: half a row step, set by menu_layout
fields.cursorY: two row steps; menu_draw adds half the font height
fields.textX: where the item numbers and labels are drawn
fields.widgetX: the widget point handed to the item draw callbacks

fields.parent: the parent node. Established by scene_node_rebuild_subtree, which branches on it: a node with zero here copies its localMatrix straight into worldMatrix, and any other node has transform_compose applied with THIS pointer + 0x3c as the outer transform - and +0x3c is worldMatrix, so the thing at +0 is a SceneNode whose composed transform this one hangs under. Typed as a plain pointer to match firstChild and nextSibling rather than as a self-reference
fields.nextSibling: and then follows this to the next child
fields.localMatrix: 3x3 orientation relative to the parent, at the module's 2^29 fixed-point scale. scene_node_set_local_matrix writes it and then sets the dirty bit, which is what distinguishes this block from the composed one at 0x3c.
fields.localX: translation relative to the parent - the tail of the local transform block. Written together by scene_node_set_origin. Called plain x/y/z until transform_copy's 0x30 fixed the block boundaries and separated local from world.
fields.worldMatrix: the composed 3x3; scene_node_transform hands out its address. Named just 'matrix' before the local block was identified.
fields.worldPos: composed translation, read out by scene_node_get_world_pos. A setter writes localX at 0x30 and a getter reads this at 0x60: two different offsets for 'position' is the direct evidence that one block is local and the other composed.
fields.userData: the world object this node carries, and the other half of a two-way link: scene_node_rebuild_subtree (formerly terrain_sub_01e400) writes the node back into userData->node, so node->userData->node is the node again. Typed WorldObject * on what the consumers do with it, not on a guess - terrain_part1 hands it straight to object_move_to_alt_list (formerly object_defer_free) and object_move_to_world_list (formerly object_remove_and_defer_free), which take one; scene_subtree_set_object_type stamps userData + 2, which is WorldObject.type; and ai_group compares object_node_userdata's result against MechEntity.avoidObstacle, which makes those two the same type. One site LOOKS like a counterexample and is not: object_node_userdata ends with node = (SceneNode *)node->userData, which reads as a node being stored here. That cast is the decompiler reusing one local for both the node it walked and the userdata it returns; the function is declared void * and returns the userdata.
fields.name: the node's name, a char pointer, or null. CONSUMER: scene_node_find_by_name stricmp's it against the name it is looking for, skipping a node whose pointer is null. The node constructors zero it (terrain_part1). DEAD IN THIS BUILD: no store of anything but 0 to it was found. The other +0x70 stores in the decompiled C are to other structs - hud_widget_init's method table, and three create paths zeroing a loadout-side field. Its one reader is unreachable too - see scene_node_find_by_name. So nodes are never looked up by name; a port can drop the field
fields.flags: bit 0 marks the node dirty - scene_node_set_local_matrix sets it on every write, so it means 'worldMatrix no longer matches localMatrix'. scene_node_walk also treats it as a leaf test.
fields.renormCountdown: calls remaining before this node's localMatrix is renormalised. scene_node_rotate_local decrements it on every incremental rotation and, at zero, calls matrix_renormalise and reseeds this from the global at 0x95ae4 - which then advances to ((old + 7) & 0x7f) + 0x40, so each node gets a different period and the work is spread across frames rather than landing on all of them at once. DO NOT EXPECT TO FIND THIS NAME IN src/: the decompiler loses the node pointer across the matrix_multiply call in that function and falls back to extraout_EBX, so the two accesses render as raw +0x78 offsets on an int. The field is real and this is where it is written; the exported body just cannot show it. RESOLVED 2026-09-25: the loss was matrix_multiply being recorded as clobbering EBX, which find_register_preservation.py no longer does, and scene_node_rotate_local now reads node->renormCountdown and node->flags

fields.polyId: the POLY resource this record's mesh is built from, or -1. world_record_build (formerly geom_poly_poly_handler) hands it straight to cache_load_resource(..., "POLY") and project_resource_size, and refuses to build when it is -1. world_record_define writes it from its second argument - the mangled id it is keyed by goes to the world record map, not here. -1 is the reset value, so a record allocated by a forward reference (the GT or TSK chunk calling world_record_alloc) and never defined keeps it; world_records_all_defined (formerly geom_table_sub_036440), called from sim_load_by_name, scans for exactly that case.
fields.blockSlot: the projectBlockFrames slot the record was defined in. world_record_build (formerly geom_poly_poly_handler) turns it into slot * 0x7c + 0x100e58, which is projectBlockFrames (0x100e10) + 0x48 - the block's composed transform - and composes that with this record's own transform at +0x48. Every caller of the handler passes this field as its second argument.
fields.parent: the parent RECORD index, or -1 or -2. world_record_define writes it and world_record_build (formerly geom_poly_poly_handler) switches on it. -2: no scene node; the block and record transforms are composed and baked into the mesh (object_transform_now (formerly geom_luma_sub_03a375)), which is static scenery. -1: an unparented node given the composed transform. Otherwise: a child of the parent record's node, placed by the local pitch/yaw/roll and pos below. world_records_propagate (formerly geom_table_sub_0362d0) reads it to carry the parent's destroyed and suppressed bits down to children, and world_record_release_subtree (formerly geom_poly_sub_036cc0) walks it to free a whole subtree.
fields.flags: packed. Bits 12..15 are the object class: the POLY handler hands (flags & 0xf000) >> 12 to object_set_class and on 5 runs object_build_ground_quadtree (formerly project_entry_sub_01cf10) - the value WorldObject.objectClass documents as the OBJ record's cls. Bits 0..8 are passed as flags & 0x1ff to poly_set_load_flags (formerly sim_objects_sub_04fee0) before the mesh loads, and object_apply_load_flags then copies bits 0-3 and 8 of that into the flags of every object the load builds, dropping 4-7. What those bits mean on the object is NOT established. world_record_define fills both from its arguments. Three state bits, all accessed as byte +0xd: 0x200 DESTROYED - gamething_destroy_world_record (formerly geom_table_sub_036240) sets it on the record a destroyed gamething points at; 0x400 GAMETHING-LINKED - set by the GT chunk's link (world_record_link_gamething (formerly geom_table_sub_0360b0)), and makes the handler tag the object with the gamething index rather than the record index; 0x800 SUPPRESSED - the handler builds nothing while it is set, 0362d0 sets it on the children of a suppressed parent and destroys their objects, and clears it again to rebuild them.
fields.objectType: the WorldObject.type the built object is given. The POLY handler writes it with object_set_type (formerly geom_luma_sub_038710), a four-instruction setter of [obj+2] - WorldObject.type - or, for a gamething-linked record, stamps it over the node's subtree with scene_subtree_set_object_type. The GT link ORs 0x200 into it, the class bits WorldObject.type already documents as gamething.
fields.replacementRecord: the record that takes this one's place when its gamething is destroyed, or -1. The GT chunk's second id is resolved to a record and stored here by world_record_link_gamething (formerly geom_table_sub_0360b0), which also sets that record's SUPPRESSED bit so it starts hidden. On destruction world_record_replace (formerly geom_table_sub_036110) marks this record DESTROYED and SUPPRESSED, destroys its object after saving the node's transform, then clears SUPPRESSED on the replacement, builds it through the POLY handler and hands it the saved transform. That the replacement is a wreck model is the obvious reading but is NOT established from the code - only that it replaces.
fields.gamething: the gameThings index linked to this record, or -1. Written by world_record_link_gamething (formerly geom_table_sub_0360b0) from the GT chunk. world_record_replace (formerly geom_table_sub_036110) indexes gameThings with it to set geomIndex to -1, and the POLY handler reads GameThing.flags bit 0x8000 through it. The reverse link is GameThing.geomIndex.
fields.object: the WorldObject built for this record, or null. The POLY handler stores poly_load_wtbo_block's result here and rebuilds when it is null. world_object_get_pos reads +0x34..+0x3c through it, which is WorldObject.posX/Y/Z; world_record_object (formerly geom_poly_sub_0367c0) returns it by record index.
fields.node: the record's scene node, or null (always null for parent -2). world_object_node returns it; world_record_define creates it as a child of the parent record's node; the POLY handler attaches the object to it.
fields.scaleX: the three scale factors world_record_build (formerly geom_poly_poly_handler) passes to poly_set_vertex_scale before loading the mesh. The reset writes 1, 1, 1.
fields.pitch: the three angles world_record_define passes as the angle arguments of matrix_from_euler_order0, whose order is documented as (out, pitch, yaw, roll, tx, ty, tz). Copied here from the same nine stack dwords as scale and pos.
fields.posX: the translation arguments of the same matrix_from_euler_order0 call. For a record with a parent record, the POLY handler passes these three to scene_node_set_origin, so they are the position relative to the parent's node.
fields.transform: the record's local transform: world_record_define builds it from pitch/yaw/roll and pos with matrix_from_euler_order0 and transform_copy's it here. For parent -2 the POLY handler composes the block frame's transform (see blockSlot) with this one, visibly at 0x101ed8 + n * 0x7c. The parent -1 branch makes the same transform_compose call, but its second argument is a register the decompiler lost track of, so that it is this field there too is likely but NOT shown. Twelve dwords, the size every transform_copy moves.
fields.tasks: head of this record's task list. world_record_task_create puts a TSK chunk's task here when the chunk names the record; world_records_run_tasks (formerly geom_table_sub_035f90) runs it with task_list_run unless the record is SUPPRESSED; world_record_replace (formerly geom_table_sub_036110) clears it with task_list_clear when the record is destroyed.

fields.boxMin: the box's low corner, x y z. From the BLK chunk's corner at +8..+0x10, moved down by the extent wherever that extent is negative, so after project_block_begin it is the minimum on every axis. Its only reader is the centre calculation below.
fields.boxMax: the box's high corner, x y z: the chunk's extent at +0x14..+0x1c, made non-negative, plus boxMin. Paired axis by axis with boxMin (+0x0c with +0x00, +0x10 with +0x04, +0x14 with +0x08). Its only reader is the centre calculation below; no consumer tests a point against the box.
fields.centre: (boxMin + boxMax) / 2 per axis. The consumer that gives it meaning is the transform build: it is the PIVOT - transform is translate by -centre, rotate by angles, translate by position, translate back by +centre - so a BLKX rotation turns the block about its own middle, not about the world origin.
fields.scale: the BLKX's integer scale per axis, copied from pendingBlockXform. DEAD: project_block_begin shifts it to 2.29 into the diagonal of a matrix it never passes to anything (0x35c63..0x35c8f), so it has no effect on the transform. defaultBlockXform makes it 1, 1, 1.
fields.angles: the BLKX's pitch, yaw, roll in 16.16 degrees. The rotation argument of matrix_from_euler_order0 in the transform build. Zero unless a BLKX preceded this BLK.
fields.position: the BLKX's x, y, z offset in cm, the translation applied after the rotation in the transform build. Zero unless a BLKX preceded this BLK.
fields.transform: the frame's full transform to world space: a 3x3 at 2^29 followed by a translation, the layout transform_point and transform_copy use. Built from the pivot, angles and position, then composed with the transform of every enclosing frame by following parent. THREE CONSUMERS: block_transform_point applies it to NAVP points; world_record_build composes it into a world record's transform; project_block_begin composes enclosing frames' copies into a new frame's.
fields.parent: the slot of the enclosing frame, or -1 at top level: project_block_begin copies projectBlockStack[depth - 1] here (the read at 0x101e0c + depth * 4, i.e. one below the new depth), and its composition loop follows it until -1.

fields.objectSlot: world_record_object_slot of the record the task's argument names, looked up through world_record_find at INIT and again on the -1 re-attach message. The tick dereferences it every frame, so a rebuilt object is followed through its slot
fields.node: object_get_node(*objectSlot), refreshed every tick; the tick sets its origin and euler angles from the smoothers and walks it. Null ends the task
fields.path: the projectPaths entry whose name matched word 3 of the task string, or null - then the first tick returns 0 and the task is removed. The tick also needs path->pointCount of at least 2
fields.startTick: the time the path was started from; the tick's elapsed time is now minus this. Mode 1 restamps it at the end of the path, mode 0 moves it on by totalDuration when it wraps, and the -1 message restamps it
fields.totalDuration: the sum of every point's duration, including the closing segment back to point 0; mode 0 subtracts it from the elapsed time to wrap
fields.rotate: 1 when word 2 was 'rotate': the tick then takes yaw from fixed_atan2 of the segment's dx, dz and pitch from fixed_asin of its dy instead of the points' own angles
fields.mode: word 1: 0 'loop' (runs on through the closing segment and wraps), 1 'repeat' (restarts at point 0 on reaching the last point), 2 anything else - MW2.PRJ writes 'oneshot' - (the tick returns 0 at the last point and the task is removed, leaving the object there)
fields.rampX: eases the node's X toward the interpolated path position (its target), 0.3 s time constant; scene_node_set_origin takes its ramp_step
fields.anglePitch: eases pitch toward the interpolated PathPoint.pitch, or the rotate-mode slope. Before each step the tick moves current by whole turns until target - current is within +-0xb40000, so it always turns the short way
fields.angleYaw: the same for yaw - PathPoint.yaw, or the rotate-mode direction of travel

fields.self: constructor stores the object's own address here
fields.visible: methods[10] sets it to 1 and methods[11] to 0. The weapon widgets' draw hook (0x2fbe0) returns at once while it is 0, and tests it again before drawing
fields.field_0x6: a per-widget short set through methods[9]; what it means depends on the widget, so it is left unnamed. On hudWidgets[0] it is a 0/1/2 state the video code branches on (vfx_video tests == 1 and == 2), and debug_command_execute (formerly target_select_section)'s key 0x73 toggles it between 0 and 1 (CORRECTION: that switch is on command id - 10, so case 0x73 is command 0x7d TOGGLE_RADAR_DAMAGE, not 0x73 - hudWidgets[0] is the radar, and this toggles its damage display); player_cockpit_frame (formerly sound_res_sub_032c50) steps a widget's value by calling methods[9] with value + 1; hud_widget_init, the constructor, zeroes it.
fields.showAfterTick: set through methods[2]. The draw hook only draws the label while simTick is greater than this, so setting it into the future hides the widget until then
fields.weaponIndex: for a weapon widget, the position of its weapon in the player's MechLoadout.weapons; -1 from the constructor otherwise. Set through methods[3]. The draw hook skips a widget with a negative value or whose weapon's type is negative, and loadout_regroup_weapons both reads it to reorder the array and rewrites it afterwards. CORRECTION: the note for this offset said it was initialised to -1 and then NEVER READ anywhere in the game code, and left it unnamed for that reason. Both readers above were missed - the draw hook is only reached through the per-instance hook pointers, and the regroup code was still untyped
fields.label: the text the widget shows. methods[4] strncpy's up to 0x20 bytes here and forces a NUL at +0x2f; loadout_regroup_weapons passes each weapon's weaponTypes[].name. The draw hook hands &label to vfx_lib_sub_058026 together with window, a font resource and the colour at 0xa4dc4
fields.window: the VFX window the widget draws into - the first argument of the draw hook's text call. methods[5] stores it and also derives the shorts at +0x40..+0x46 from the window's {x0, y0, x1, y1} at +4..+0x10 as x, y, x1 - x0 + 1 and y1 - y0 + 1; methods[8] sets those four directly. No reader of the four has been seen, so they stay unnamed. CORRECTION: readers exist and they are named now (left, top, width, height) - see those fields for the consumers
fields.textPos: set through methods[6] (hud_widget_store_34); hud_widgets_install passes 0x96ac0 + i * 8, two ints per widget. CONSUMER: hud_weapon_widget_tick reads [textPos] and [textPos + 4] and pushes them as the x and y of its string draw (vfx_lib_sub_058026, 0x2fb8b..0x2fb95). The image values (4588, 8520 on the weapon widgets; 58982, 42598 on others) are not pixel positions; they look like 16.16 fractions that the start-up rescale turns into pixels, which is not verified
fields.paneTransition: set through methods[7] (hud_widget_store_38) from 0x96bc0[i]: non-null only on hudWidgets[2] (0x96bb8) and [13] (0x96ba0). A pair {state, params}: state bytes {now, before} and an int elapsed at +2; params {duration, fromPane, toPane, outPane}. CONSUMERS: the widgets' hooks[0] and hooks[2] restart it (vfx_font_sub_014aa0) and step it (vfx_font_sub_014c50), which interpolates outPane between the two panes over duration ticks - first the horizontal edges, then the vertical - and the hook draws the widget into the result: the display opening while the mech powers up and closing otherwise
fields.lastStatus: the playerStatusCopy the widget's hook last ran under, stored at the end of every hooks[0], [2] and [3] of hudWidgets[2] and [13]. CONSUMERS: hooks[0] restarts the pane transition unless lastStatus is 1, and hooks[2] unless it is 0, 3 or 4 - so each transition starts once, on the frame the status changes
fields.left: the widget box's left edge, window x0 (methods[5]). CONSUMER: hud_damage_display_init centres the damage diagram at left + (width - shape width) / 2 - which is what fixes these four as a box
fields.top: the box's top edge, window y0; hud_damage_display_init centres vertically at top + (height - shape height) / 2
fields.width: x1 - x0 + 1, the box width in pixels; also read by damage_sub_030fc0 (the mode-2 bar layout) and the ai_group_part1 HUD code to size and clamp what they draw
fields.height: y1 - y0 + 1, the box height; read beside width by the same consumers
fields.methods: twelve entry points the constructor fills in; slot 0 is the constructor itself. All eleven others are one- or two-line accessors (0x2f090..0x2f180): [1] no-op, [2] showAfterTick, [3] weaponIndex, [4] label, [5] window plus rect, [6] +0x34, [7] +0x38, [8] rect, [9] +0x06, [10] show, [11] hide
fields.hooks: left null by the constructor and patched per instance by hud_widgets_install - this is the overridable part. They are DRAW callbacks: every frame player_cockpit_frame (formerly sound_res_sub_032c50) switches on the display mode at 0xfe1a4 and calls hooks[0] of all 24 widgets in mode 1, hooks[1] in mode 2 and hooks[2] otherwise.CORRECTION: 0xfe1a4 is not a display mode but playerStatusCopy, the player's MechLoadout.status - so the HUD draws hooks[0] while the mech powers up (1), hooks[1] while it runs (2) and hooks[2] otherwise (just spawned, shut down). What the modes are is not established

fields.torso_tilt: analog, range -60..60, stored 16.16 (value << 16) - input_poll_controls writes it with shift 0
fields.torso_pan: analog, range -90..90, stored 16.16 (value << 16) - input_poll_controls writes it with shift 0
fields.throttle: analog, range 0..1024, stored as a plain integer - input_poll_controls shifts it right by 16
fields.legsPan: not in the channel table, so not bindable. ai_steer_heading writes it proportional to the heading error, saturating at +/-0x3333333 beyond 45 degrees, and ai_choose_throttle reads it back as the turn magnitude.
fields.legs_pan_delta: analog, range -1024..1024, stored 16.16 (value << 16) - input_poll_controls writes it with shift 0
fields.reverseDirection: not in the channel table, so not bindable as a channel; it is a keyboard command instead. The name is the game's own: gamekey.map's parser (input.c) looks command names up in the {name, id} table at 0x9dca4, where REVERSE_DIRECTION carries id 0x3f, and command_execute (formerly option_toggle) case 0x3f flips playerControls +0x2f between 0 and 1. CONSUMERS: mech_anim_select_gait (formerly terrain_sub_01f4f0) sets animTarget to 2 whenever it is set, overriding the speed-band choice; hud_gauge_throttle draws -throttle/2 instead of throttle; netplay sends it as bit 7 of the state byte. The AI sets it in behaviours 8 and 10 (10 is entered when blocked) and ai_exit_behaviour clears it; ai_blocked_ends_behaviour and the same test inlined in ai_choose_behaviour do not count a reversing mech as stuck; ai_handle_blocked and ai_pursue_target skip the look-ahead obstacle probe while it is set. NOT FOUND: no read of it in the velocity integration. A capstone sweep of every Ghidra-known game function for byte accesses at [reg+0x2f] or 0x98373 finds 16, all of them the ones listed here - but code outside known function bodies was not swept, so how reversing actually moves the mech backwards is not established. RESOLVED later: it works through the animation state, never read directly. mech_anim_select_gait (formerly terrain_sub_01f4f0) turns this flag into animTarget 2, and mech_std_tick_ai, finding animState == 2, sets the forward-speed ramp's target (MechLoadout.ramps[2]) to -target/2. That speed is what mech_std_tick_terrain turns into velocity, so reverse runs at half the forward speed. That is also why the throttle gauge draws -throttle/2.
fields.nextObjective: a keyboard command, not a channel - the byte between the channel table's inspect_target (0x3a) and advance_gamething (0x3c). The name is the game's: in the gamekey.map command table at 0x9dca4 NEXT_OBJECTIVE is id 0x4b, and command_execute (formerly option_toggle) case 0x4b sets this byte to 1. The neighbouring id checks the mapping: 0x4a is TARGET_LAST_SHOT and case 0x4a sets the target_last_shot channel. CONSUMER: mech_std_tick_ai, finding it set, calls ai_cycle_target(entity, 1, 0x10008) and clears it - the same routine the other target-cycling commands use, with a filter argument of 0x10008. What that filter selects is not established here; the command name says objectives. RESOLVED: 0x10008 admits mechs with MechEntity.flags 0x40 (none in MW2.PRJ, no writer found) and - because ai_validate_gamething's 0x10000 test is dead - every gamething, so the key cycles the same set as advance_gamething. See ai_cycle_target.
fields.cheatJumpjets: set only by cheat_handle_command, in the branch that posts 'Jumpjets' when its (obfuscated) code matches; nothing clears it. CONSUMER: mech_std_tick_ai, whenever MechLoadout.jumpFuel is -2 and this is set, gives the mech working jets - jumpFuel 0x71c, jumpCapacity 3, jetDeltaY gravity * 3. -2 is what mech_config writes for a chassis whose jump value is 0, and what mech_damage_slot writes when certain equipment is destroyed. So the cheat fits jets to a mech that has none and refits them after damage. It does not touch the -1 case, a negative chassis value.

fields.type: the objective type bit; copied to the runtime record. Record 0 must be 0x10 (start) or objective_table_install fatal-errors (system_error 0x4a)
fields.listed: 'V' = shown on the objectives screen; the installer stores (listed == 'V')
fields.prereqAll: non-zero: every prerequisite must hold; zero: any. Copied to Objective.prereqAll
fields.prereqs: eight 4-byte prerequisites: condition char ('C' completed -> 1, 'S' succeeded -> 2, 'F' failed -> 3, else 0), then the objective's record and table indices. The installer maps the char and copies the two bytes into Objective.prerequisites
fields.timeLimit: seconds of missionSeconds, -1 for none; copied to Objective.timeLimit
fields.category: the category byte the objectives screen filters on; copied to the runtime record
fields.isPrerequisite: 'M' = a type-0x20 objective waits for this one; the installer stores (== 'M') into Objective.isPrerequisite, whose name this takes (dump_objectives' 'req' column). Briefly named required when first declared
fields.membersPerTarget: copied to Objective.membersPerTarget (+0x61), whose name this takes (dump_objectives' 'quota' column): group_assign_objective_task sends members at each target until this many are on it, 0 meaning every member. Briefly named quota when first declared
fields.restraint: copied to Objective.restraint: 1 hold task (aiFlags 0x42), 2 do not engage (0x41)
fields.successSound: TABL name of the success announcement, resolved through SNDTABLE (resource_id_by_name(0xb)) and copied with its id
fields.failureSound: TABL name of the failure announcement; as successSound
fields.targetStreamName: the name of the mission stream whose placed objects become this objective's TARGETS. READER: mission_mark_by_name stricmps its argument - the running stream's own name - against missionTables[t] + i * 0x97 + 0x70, which is 0x26 + 0x4a into record i, and marks each match state 7 (open for targets); mission_record_add_value then appends the stream's GT/GP/NAVP objects. dump_objectives.py prints it as 'ident'. CORRECTION: this was declared unnamed as having no consumer, because objective_table_install does not copy it - the reader works on the static chunk, not the runtime record. CHECKED against MW2.PRJ (dump_objectives.py, line 2 of objectives.txt): of 1832 non-empty values, 1412 name a BWD stream in the file, 226 a loose .BWD beside it (USERSTAR, EN01STAR..EN05STAR - the player's and enemy stars, which project_open_stream (formerly project_lookup_id) loads as files), 189 are NULL, and 5 name nothing found
fields.actionTable: for action types, the table the action applies to; copied to Objective.actionTable
fields.actionObjective: for action types, the objective in actionTable; copied to Objective.actionObjective
fields.text: the objective's text, NUL-terminated; copied to Objective.text

fields.posX: the camera's world position. Read straight off viewerPosition by the sound and effect code - mech_play_anim_transition_sound computes mech->posX - *(int *)viewerPosition and the two neighbours at +4 and +8 for y and z, which is what fixes this triple and proves the record is not a MechEntity.
fields.yaw: the camera's heading, in the sim's usual 16.16 degrees, measured the same way vec_to_range_bearing's azimuth is - from +Z toward +X. FOUR consumers agree, and the decisive one has nothing to do with the camera code: sound_pan_from_bearing computes fixed_sin(viewerPosition->yaw - sourceAzimuth) and maps it to a Miles stereo pan of 0..127 about a centre of 0x40. Stereo panning is a purely horizontal quantity - a pitch cannot produce it - so this is the axis the camera turns about vertically. The other three: the chase camera in camera_orbit_update ramps this straight to vec_to_range_bearing's outAzimuth to aim at what it follows; the free camera in camera_free_fly takes fixed_sin and fixed_cos of it and multiplies them into posX and posZ to walk along the ground, and never clamps it, so it wraps; and camera_eject_view spins it by 300 per tick while the camera rises. CORRECTION: this was a three-int array called orientation, whose comment said 'WHICH ANGLE IS WHICH AXIS IS NOT ESTABLISHED ... orientation[0] and [1] is honest; pitch and yaw would not be.' That was the right call on the evidence then available. It is established now, and the old note was not wrong about anything except how much was known - the array form itself carried no false claim.
fields.pitch: how far the camera is tilted off the horizontal, same 16.16 degrees, POSITIVE LOOKING DOWN. Three consumers, and the sign comes from the first of them. The chase camera ramps this to the NEGATED outElevation of vec_to_range_bearing - -(trim) - elevation - and elevation there is fixed_atan2(dy, groundRange) of the vector from the camera TO the subject, so a subject below the camera gives a negative elevation and a positive pitch. camera_free_fly clamps it to +/-0x5a0000 and nothing else: a quarter turn each way is the classic pitch stop, and it is applied to this field while yaw beside it is left free to wrap. camera_eject_view settles the sign - it writes exactly +0x5a0000 once on entry and then pins posX and posZ to the subject while accelerating posY upward, which is a camera climbing away while looking straight down at what it left.
fields.roll: the camera roll. ESTABLISHED as of the euler-order work; this note previously read NAMED BY ELIMINATION and warned it was worth suspicion, which was right at the time. viewer_build_transform pushes this field into the THIRD angle slot of matrix_from_euler_order0, which is the roll slot - see scene_node_get_world_euler. Still true, and still worth knowing: reading - exactly the footing MechEntity.torsoRoll is on, and worth the same suspicion. Nothing computes it and nothing branches on it. Two camera modes write it 0 on entry (camera_orbit_update and camera_free_fly), vfx_font and render_asm_part2 copy and difference it componentwise beside yaw and pitch, and that is every access. With the other two axes established, roll is what is left of an orientation triple, and a camera that never banks explains why it is always zero - but no consumer says so.
fields.zoom: the view magnification, 16.16, with 0x10000 as unity. Three consumers agree. viewer_update_projection clamps it to 0x8000..0x100000 - half to sixteen times - and multiplies aspectScale by it to build the projection. vfx_video takes fixed_atan2(0x10000, zoom), which is the half-angle of the field of view that magnification implies. And ai_group_part1 saves it, substitutes its own value for one render and puts the old one back, which is what a temporary zoom override looks like. camera_apply_zoom (formerly geom_luma_sub_039440) picks between two preset globals, stores the result here, and on a change raises the redraw flag at 0x954ec and plays sound 0x147 - the click of a zoom step. BEWARE how that function reads: it appears to store a CODE POINTER, "*(undefined **)&viewerPosition->field_0x18 = puVar2", and to set its presets to &LAB_00010000. That is a decompiler artefact, not a pointer. The code object begins at 0x00010000, so the immediate 0x10000 - which is simply 1.0 in 16.16 - is a valid code address and Ghidra renders it as a label. Any 0x10000 constant in this binary can surface the same way.
fields.lightPos: THE SCENE LIGHT: its world position, in cm, or its direction when lightDirectional is set. The decisive consumer is poly_light_intensity. viewer_latch_globals copies the three words to 0x14fec0, 0x14fec4 and 0x14feb8, and poly_light_intensity subtracts a polygon's first vertex from them and dots the result with the face normal. WRITERS: the LITE chunk (keyword light) stores chunk +0x10..+0x18 here for the static viewer at 0x96f3c (0x96f58 = 0x96f3c + 0x1c). Each frame vfx_video sets it from world_object_get_pos(lightObjectRecord) while lightObjectFollow is on, which a LITO chunk (lightobj) arranges. effect_spawn moves it to an explosion for the effect's lifetime (EffectType.lightsScene). effect_spawn also compares it with posX/posZ, to keep the nearer of two lights. IN MW2.PRJ the 46 LITE chunks put it, for example, at (1000, 20000, 0), 200 m up. CORRECTION: named targetPos, 'a second world position the camera code measures itself against', with its purpose left open. It is not a camera position or a look-at point.
fields.lightDirectional: non-zero: lightPos is a DIRECTION, and every polygon sees the same light vector. Zero: it is a POINT, and the vector is lightPos minus the polygon's first vertex. Consumer: poly_light_intensity, through the copy viewer_latch_globals makes at 0x14fcb8, which replaces the vertex position by 0 when this is set. The LITE chunk writes it from chunk +0x1e, and it is 0 or 1 in all 46 LITE chunks. effect_spawn clears it while an explosion is the light and restores it afterwards.
fields.ambientLight: the AMBIENT floor of the lighting, on a 0..128 scale. light_shade_level, through the copy at 0x14fcbc, mixes a face's light intensity as amb + intensity x (128 - amb) / 128. So 128 makes lighting irrelevant and 0 lets faces edge-on to the light go black. The LITE chunk writes it from chunk +0x1c; in MW2.PRJ the values run from 0 to 95. effect_spawn lowers it by 10 while an explosion is the light, so the flash stands out, resets it to 0x40 if the result falls outside 0..255, and restores it afterwards.
fields.left: the viewport rectangle. viewport_select writes 0 here and into top, and the chosen mode's width and height into right and bottom; viewer_update_projection then averages left with right and top with bottom to get centreX and centreY, and halves their differences into halfWidth and halfHeight. Two functions pairing them the same way is what makes this a rectangle rather than four loose numbers.
fields.nearClip: the near clip distance, in view-space depth units. Established from the CONSUMER, not from how it is derived: viewer_project_point (formerly render_asm_sub_03f320) projects each vertex onto the third row of rotation to get a view-space depth, caches it on the vertex, and then sets bit 0 of the vertex flags when that depth is below nearClip x 4 and bit 1 when it is above farClip x 4. It ANDs those flags across the polygon and drops the polygon when every vertex agrees - the standard outcode reject against a near and a far plane. The x 4 is a unit conversion, not a margin: the rotation rows are at the 2^29 scale this binary uses for scene-node matrices and the dot product is shifted right by 27, so the depth comes out four times world units. viewer_latch_globals copies both bounds into the render globals in both forms, exactly as it does for left/right/top/bottom. viewer_set_near_clip writes it. viewer_update_projection gives it a default of (zoom x halfWidth) >> 17 + 1 - focalScale scaled down - but that derivation is NOT what names the field; it is only where the default comes from. The VIEW chunk's +8 is stored here too (0x4e74d), 64 in all 46 chunks. It has NO EFFECT on a mission: main calls vfx_font_sub_014950 right after sim_load_by_name, which calls viewer_update_projection, and that overwrites this field with its own default. A port can drop it.
